title: AI-Assisted Identity and Access Threat Detection Using the AITIR Framework for Public-Sector Cybersecurity Environments
abstract: In public-sector cybersecurity, the password has become the prize. Agencies have moved their services into the cloud and now hand out access to employees, contractors, and members of the public alike, and that change has dragged the fight off the network perimeter and onto the credential itself. We describe AITIR, short for Adaptive Identity-and-access Threat Intelligence and Response, a layered machine-learning framework that watches for identity-based attacks as they happen and coordinates a response inside the governance rules agencies already have to follow. Three models share the detection work: a gradient-boosted classifier reads each access attempt, a bidirectional sequence model reads the order of an account's actions, and a graph-based behavior-analytics module flags the moment a session drifts away from an identity's usual company. Sitting on top of them, an explainable triage layer passes only the high-confidence, well-justified alerts to a person. To test the design, we assembled a corpus of about 14.8 million authentication and access events, part public benchmark data and part synthetic identity telemetry, and pushed credential stuffing, password spraying, privilege escalation, session hijacking, and insider misuse through it. AITIR scored an F1 of 0.967 and an area under the ROC curve of 0.985, ahead of all five baselines. Over a four-quarter deployment simulation it cut successful identity-based intrusions by 31.4 percent, brought mean time to detect down by 62 percent, and trimmed false positives by 41 percent against a conventional operations baseline. A cost-benefit model, scaled to a national public-sector portfolio, points to roughly US$10.2 billion in avoided cost a year and about 79,000 analyst hours given back. Those last two numbers are projections built on stated assumptions, not audited savings, and we say so plainly. The paper closes on the governance, staffing, and validity questions that decide whether any of them survives contact with a real agency.

abstract: This article consolidates the validation of the Intuition Ecosystem Model (IEM) as a disruptive governance infrastructure. Grounded in the integration of human neurophysiology and complex systems theory (Balloni, 2022), the IEM Model optimizes decision-making under extreme uncertainty. The validation of this Model is presented through a multidimensional lens: (i) structural, via Self-Organizing Holarchic Open Systems (SOHO); (ii) biological, through the 'somatic congruence' metric; and (iii) ethical, grounded in the concept of Ecoism. This work culminates in the Balloni Protocol, an auditable procedural flow that harmonizes algorithmic precision with biological wisdom. By synthesizing these structural, biological, and ethical dimensions, the study provides a robust technical blueprint for contemporary governance, ensuring that technological integration enhances human sovereign intelligence and effectively mitigates the systemic risks of cognitive atrophy in automated governance.

title: Risk Aversion: A Narrative Review
abstract: Several effects have been noted for risk aversion including risk – reducing behaviors, social distancing, staying at home, distress and gambling disorder. A few predictors of risk aversion have been noted in this current literature including social activity, social standing and incentives to work. Several risk factors for risk aversion have also appeared in this literature. They include background uncertainty, induced worry, depression, less dopamine, less testosterone, schizophrenia and multiple risk factors. Methodological limitations include the almost exclusive sampling of participants with clinical conditions including anxiety, depression, schizophrenia and dementia. In addition, most of the studies are cross-sectional versus longitudinal, thus limiting any directionality conclusions.

title: Healthcare Workers’ Preparedness for Monkeypox Pandemic Response in SubSaharan Africa: A Rapid Review Investigating the Knowledge Gap
abstract: Background: Mpox is a zoonotic viral disease caused by an Orthopoxvirus endemic to sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), where its resurgence underscores the urgent need for improved preparedness among health care workers (HCWs). Despite the potential of a One Health approach, current implementations remain fragmented. This rapid review synthesises evidence on HCWs' knowledge, attitudes, information sources, and barriers to preparedness regarding Mpox in SSA to identify training needs and policy implications. Methods: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, PubMed and ScienceDirect were searched using MeSH terms and Boolean operators for studies published between 2000 and 2024. Studies assessing HCW knowledge, attitudes, or preparedness for Mpox in SSA with full-text availability in English or French were included; those involving non-HCW populations, conducted outside SSA, or lacking primary data were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data using a standardised template; quality was assessed using the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical CrossSectional Studies. Results: Five studies from 388 records were included (Cameroon, Ethiopia, Nigeria, DRC; n = 1,672 HCWs). Only 46.8% of HCWs demonstrated adequate Mpox knowledge. Barriers included reliance on social media and limited access to formal training. Positive attitudes towards prevention correlated with higher knowledge levels. Conclusion: Fewer than half of SSA HCWs demonstrate adequate Mpox knowledge despite a regional case fatality rate nearly ten times the global average; positive attitudes are not translating into clinical preparedness, reflecting a critical intention-action gap; and social media dominates as an information source, underscoring the need for peer-reviewed alternatives within a One Health training framework.

title: Evaluating Software Quality Through Automated Testing and Predictive Defect Detection Using Machine Learning
abstract: Software quality assurance increasingly depends on the ability to combine automated testing with data-driven estimates of defect risk. Conventional test suites reveal failures in executed scenarios but do not necessarily identify which untested changes are most likely to introduce faults. Machine learning models can prioritize code review and testing by learning associations between historical defect outcomes, code structure, change activity, and process characteristics. This narrative review synthesizes established research on software defect prediction and proposes a transparent evaluation framework integrating data preparation, temporal validation, calibrated prediction, risk-based test selection, and continuous monitoring. It distinguishes test effectiveness from model discrimination and emphasizes precision–recall analysis, operational cost, data leakage prevention, and human oversight. A conceptual graph illustrates how testing effort might be redistributed according to predicted risk; it does not represent measured experimental outcomes. The paper argues that machine learning should supplement rather than replace automated tests, and that deployment claims require prospective, project-specific evidence. Limitations include incomplete defect labels, shifting development practices, class imbalance, and uncertain cross-project transferability

title: Integrating digital competence and TPACK in physics teaching: A systematic literature review
abstract: This study aims to examine research trends in teachers' digital competence and Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK), identify factors influencing their development, and explore their implications for physics education. A systematic literature review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Relevant studies were retrieved from Scopus and Google Scholar, yielding 325 records. Following the initial screening, 100 records were assessed based on their titles and abstracts, and 12 articles met the inclusion criteria for narrative and thematic synthesis. The findings reveal varying levels of digital competence and TPACK among teachers, with professional training, teaching experience, and access to technological resources emerging as key influencing factors. In physics education, these competencies support the integration of digital technologies to visualize abstract concepts, facilitate conceptual understanding, and enhance instructional practices. However, the limited number of physics-specific studies and the predominance of self-reported data constrain the generalizability of the findings. Future research should prioritize empirical investigations in physics education and develop context-specific instruments to assess teachers' digital competence and TPACK. This review highlights the importance of targeted professional development and adequate technological support in strengthening technology-integrated physics instruction.

title: Advancing Rigorous and Inclusive Health Research for a Resilient Global Future
abstract: The evolving global health landscape presents a complex interplay of opportunities and challenges, requiring robust, interdisciplinary, and policy-relevant research to guide effective decision-making. This editorial introduces Health Research Review (HRR) as a scholarly platform committed to advancing high-quality research across clinical, public, and global health domains. It highlights the critical need to bridge the gap between evidence generation and real-world application, particularly in low- and middle-income contexts where systemic constraints often limit the implementation of evidence-based interventions. The editorial emphasises the importance of integrating diverse disciplines—ranging from medicine and epidemiology to health economics and behavioural sciences—to address multifaceted health issues. It further underscores the journal’s commitment to methodological rigour, ethical integrity, and global inclusivity in promoting impactful research. By fostering dialogue among researchers, practitioners, and policymakers, HRR aims to strengthen health systems, inform equitable policies, and support sustainable improvements in population health. The editorial also outlines emerging priorities, including digital health innovation, climate-related health risks, and health system resilience, positioning HRR as a forward-looking forum for transformative health research.

title: Effects of Dynamic, Static and Post-Activation Warm-Up Strategies on Athletic Performance: A Narrative Review
abstract: Warm-up is widely recognized as a fundamental component of athletic preparation and is commonly used to enhance performance and reduce injury risk. Various warm-up strategies have been investigated in recent years, including dynamic warm-up, static stretching, Post-Activation Performance Enhancement (PAPE), foam rolling, and plyometric exercises. However, the relative effectiveness of these approaches remains unclear. The aim of this narrative review was to synthesize current evidence regarding the effects of different warm-up strategies on athletic performance and injury prevention. A literature search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar databases, and studies published between 2015 and 2025 were considered. Twenty-two studies met the inclusion criteria. The findings indicated that dynamic warm-up produced the most consistent improvements in sprint performance, agility, jumping ability, and sport-specific skills. PAPE protocols were also associated with enhanced power output and explosive performance. Static stretching primarily improved flexibility and range of motion, whereas foam rolling showed limited effects on performance despite increasing mobility. Plyometric warmup strategies yielded mixed results. In addition, structured warm-up programs incorporating balance, strength, and neuromuscular exercises contributed to injury prevention and improved postural control. Overall, the available evidence suggests that dynamic warm-up and PAPE protocols currently represent the most effective evidence-based strategies for enhancing athletic performance, while structured warm-up programs play an important role in injury prevention.

title: <b>Critical Issues in Building Information Modeling (BIM) Workflows: A Multi-Case Study Review</b>
abstract: Building Information Modeling (BIM) is increasingly used in structural and infrastructure engineering as a digital environment supporting design, construction, and asset management processes. However, the application of BIM to complex infrastructures still presents several critical issues, particularly when dealing with non-standard geometries, existing structures, and heterogeneous information flows. This paper presents a technical synthesis based on six case studies developed by the authors through BIM-based approaches applied to different structural and infrastructural fields, including bridges, road infrastructures, underground utility networks, and complex structural systems. The study analyzes the main issues encountered during the modeling, coordination, and data exchange phases, highlighting the strategies adopted to address them. The identified challenges mainly concern the geometric modeling of irregular or existing structures, interoperability issues between BIM software and structural analysis software, the management of point clouds and survey-derived data, as well as the definition of appropriate Levels of Development and Information. The paper provides a technical overview of recurring issues and offers useful indications for improving BIM workflows applied to structural and infrastructure engineering.

title: An Inventory Model for Non-Instantaneously Reasoned, Continuously Deteriorating Items under a Linear Demand Rate
abstract: This paper develops a deterministic economic order quantity (EOQ) model for a single deteriorating item under a linear, time-dependent demand rate D(t) = a+bt, where deterioration proceeds at a constant instantaneous rate θ applied to the on-hand inventory. Shortages are not permitted. The governing first-order linear differential equation describing inventory depletion is solved in closed form, and the order quantity, holding cost integral, and deterioration cost expression are derived analytically and verified symbolically. The average total cost per unit time, TCU(T), is shown via a rigorous second-order condition together with numerical evidence to be strictly convex in the cycle length T, guaranteeing a unique global minimizer T∗. The model is further validated by showing that it reduces exactly to the classical no-deterioration linear-trend model as θ →0, to the constant-demand Ghare–Schrader deteriorating inventory model as b→0, and to the textbook economic order quantity formula as both θ →0 and b→0 simultaneously. A solution algorithm is proposed, and a numerical example, together with an extended six-scenario numerical study spanning low, base, and high deterioration rates and growing, flat, and declining demand trends, and a comprehensive sensitivity analysis with respect to the deterioration rate, demand trend, holding cost, deterioration cost, and ordering cost, illustrates the practical behaviour of the optimal policy across realistic operating regimes. Managerial insights and limitations relevant to perishable goods and fast-moving consumer goods supply chains are discussed in detail.

title: <b>Teaching Data Cleaning in Machine Learning: A Misconception-Driven Pedagogical Framework for Explainable and Ethical Data Preprocessing </b>
abstract: Data cleaning — the process of detecting and remedying missing, erroneous, and inconsistent records in raw datasets — is widely recognized as the most time-consuming and consequential stage of the machine learning preprocessing pipeline. Yet despite its operational centrality, how data cleaning should be taught to undergraduate computer science students has received remarkably little systematic attention in the machine learning education literature. This paper addresses that gap by developing a theoretically grounded pedagogical framework for instructors teaching data cleaning in higher education contexts. Drawing on threshold concept theory, constructivist learning principles, and the documented landscape of machine learning education challenges, we identify three pervasive misconceptions: the deletion reflex, the imputation neutrality fallacy, and the outlier criminalization fallacy. We propose a four-phase instructional sequence — Motivational Grounding, Mechanism Diagnosis, Algorithm-Context Mapping, and Explainability and Ethical Reflection — operationalized through a multi-dimensional Instructor Cleaning Strategy Matrix. The framework is empirically grounded through a case study applying the full technique repertoire to a real-world academic email dataset of over 10,000 records spanning eleven years. A cross-method comparison demonstrates that imputation methods produced NRMSE values ranging from 0.08 to 0.45, and anomaly detection methods flagged between 185 and 412 records on identical data. Implications for machine learning curriculum design, assessment, and data ethics literacy are discussed. By embedding explainability and ethical reflection as a mandatory fourth phase of instruction — grounded in GDPR, the EU AI Act, and ISO 8000 requirements — the framework equips learners to navigate the data governance demands of contemporary technology-enhanced professional environments.

title: Technology Research Review: Advancing Interdisciplinary Scholarship in Technological Innovation, Digital Transformation, and Emerging Intelligent Systems
abstract: The rapid evolution of modern technologies has transformed industrial systems, governance structures, and societal interactions, creating an urgent need for rigorous and interdisciplinary scholarly inquiry. The Technology Research Review (TRR), published by SPIDER Publishing, is an international peer-reviewed journal dedicated to advancing high-quality research in technological innovation, applied systems, and digital transformation. This editorial outlines the journal’s vision to serve as a global platform for theoretical, empirical, experimental, and applied research across diverse domains, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, big data analytics, cybersecurity, blockchain technologies, Internet of Things, robotics, smart manufacturing, and sustainable technologies. TRR emphasizes methodological rigor, originality, and real-world applicability while promoting cross-disciplinary integration among engineering, computer science, data science, and innovation studies. The journal also highlights emerging frontiers such as quantum computing, digital twins, advanced materials, and AI governance, while critically engaging with ethical, regulatory, and societal implications of technological advancement. By fostering research that bridges scientific discovery and practical implementation, TRR aims to contribute to sustainable, inclusive, and responsible technological progress globally. The editorial underscores the journal’s commitment to shaping a knowledge ecosystem that informs academia, industry innovation, and policy development in the era of digital transformation.

title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Secure Healthcare Data Analysis in Distributed Computing Environments
abstract: Healthcare analytics increasingly depends on geographically distributed clinical records, connected medical devices, imaging repositories, and institutional data platforms. Conventional centralized learning can increase exposure of sensitive information and amplify governance challenges when data must cross organizational boundaries. Federated learning offers a collaborative alternative in which participating sites train local models and exchange updates rather than raw records. However, model updates can still disclose private information, and operational heterogeneity can compromise accuracy, fairness, and reliability. This narrative review develops a privacy-preserving federated learning framework for secure healthcare data analysis, combining local preprocessing, identity and consent controls, secure aggregation, differential privacy, authenticated communication, robust aggregation, and continuous audit. It evaluates design trade-offs across clinical utility, confidentiality, interoperability, deployment cost, and reproducibility. The proposed framework is conceptual rather than an experimentally validated implementation; its evaluation criteria and illustrative figure are intended to guide future empirical studies. A governance-centered design is recommended in which technical protections complement clinical oversight and institutional accountability.

title: Blockchain-Based Authentication and Access Control for Secure Cloud Computing Infrastructure
abstract: Cloud computing concentrates valuable workloads behind identity services, administrative interfaces, and machine-to-machine authorization channels. Centralized access records can be difficult to reconcile across providers and may create single points of administrative failure. Blockchain-based designs offer tamper-evident policy history, shared verification, and programmable authorization, but they also introduce consensus delays, governance burdens, privacy exposure, and smart-contract risks. This narrative review evaluates an architecture in which permissioned ledger services register identity commitments and access-policy versions while sensitive attributes, credentials, and workload data remain off-chain. The paper discusses decentralized identifiers, verifiable credentials, challenge-response authentication, role- and attribute-based authorization, revocation, privacy-preserving evidence, cloud integration, and realistic security evaluation. Rather than presenting invented performance measurements, it proposes testable research questions, threat scenarios, and comparison baselines for assessing whether a ledger materially improves security over conventional identity and access management. The principal conclusion is that blockchain can improve cross-organizational auditability in some settings but is not a substitute for secure identity proofing, key custody, sound policy engineering, or operational monitoring.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Improving Transparency and Reliability in Automated Decision-Making Systems
abstract: Automated decision-making systems increasingly influence healthcare, finance, recruitment, education, public administration, and digital platforms. Although advanced machine-learning models can discover complex relationships, their opaque reasoning can obstruct auditing, contestability, and safe deployment. This narrative review examines how explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) may improve transparency and reliability by clarifying model behavior, revealing data dependencies, supporting error detection, and enabling informed human oversight. It synthesizes established work on interpretable modeling, local feature attribution, surrogate explanations, counterfactual reasoning, explanation evaluation, and governance. A conceptual assurance framework connects data provenance, predictive validation, explanation fidelity, subgroup analysis, and operational monitoring. The paper distinguishes understandable explanations from evidence that a system is accurate, robust, or fair: an attractive explanation alone does not establish reliability. A non-empirical diagram illustrates complementary assurance dimensions without implying measured results. Practical implications include tailoring explanations to decision recipients, testing explanation stability under perturbations, documenting uncertainty, and establishing appeal mechanisms. The review concludes that XAI is most effective when embedded within a wider socio-technical accountability process rather than deployed as a stand-alone visualization technique.

title: Text, Duality and the Bidirectional Semantic Knowledge: An EpistemicMathematical Model for Semantics
abstract: In this article, we present an epistemic-mathematical duality frame for universality-to-text and text-into-text semantics from our approach with focus on the nature of semantic knowledge implying hypotheses and results of computational brain dimensions of the latter. Thus, starting from a space mathematical organization of language on the linguistic object, especially duality of self-expansion/self-reduction, a threefold attempt enables the following: First, we rely on axiomatic frames of abstract semantic algebra and its representation-induction model. Secondly, by means of demonstration, a test along with two major components is proposed in which the first component verifies SOP (conceptual)/POS (compositional) logical-semantic implications of syntax-semantic duality: a model of state/term absorption is applied (XConceptual compositional). Furthermore, we present a graph model of duality based on perfect elimination ordering PEO between conceptual and compositional dualities endowed with polarity and reversibility. Moreover, a model of participational duality entails an experimental/empirical framework through conversational interactions. From diplo/haplo-arguments, cognitive duality of intelligibility/comprehension yields an epistemic function from Conceptual Wholes and Conceptual absorption/inversion specified by Labeled or regressive Constatives Lco and interpretive primitives IP (through Gamma function). Lastly, a debate on semantic holism and duality suggests a dual oriented holism of the bidirectional text OTO.

title: Kekerasan dalam Mendisiplinkan Anak: Telaah Batasan dan Celah dalam Pertanggungjawaban Pidana di Indonesia
abstract: In Indonesian positive law, the prohibition of all forms of child abuse is not only present as a legal norm, but also as a moral commitment of the state to guarantee the dignity and safety of children. However, the reality on the ground shows that violence against children still often occurs in closed domestic spaces. Some of these acts are justified on the grounds of discipline, as if the use of physical violence were a legitimate tool in the parenting process. This study aims to identify and understand the precise limits of physical violence that is justified as child discipline under Indonesian positive law and to determine whether there are legal loopholes that allow parental violence in the context of discipline to go unpunished. This study uses normative legal research, an approach that centres legal texts and norms. Indonesian positive law, in principle, prohibits all forms of violence against children. However, the regulations do not provide a clear limit on which disciplinary actions remain justifiable. In other words, the legal boundaries exist normatively, but are not explicitly and operationally articulated so that they can be easily applied in practice. When these provisions are applied in practice, it is clear that there are still significant ambiguities and legal loopholes, namely, the absence of a definition or limitation of discipline in positive law. The existence of room for subjective interpretation by officials and judges. Socio-cultural constructs that still legitimise corporal punishment. The linking of violent offences to the element of injury, so that 'minor' violence often goes unpunished. The absence of explicit norms prohibiting physical violence as a form of child discipline. The lack of consistent law enforcement guidelines and jurisprudence. It is this law that opens up the possibility of impunity, namely, the suboptimal criminal accountability of perpetrators of violence who hide behind the excuse of discipline.

title: <b>From Design to Discovery: A Systematic Review of Canva AI as a Pedagogical Tool in Education </b>
abstract: The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in education has drawn attention to digital learning tools that support creativity and effective teaching. Canva is originally a graphic design platform that evolved into an AI-assisted education tool. This study conducted a systematic review following the PRISMA guidelines and the SPIDER framework to explore Canva’s role in secondary education, focusing on its uses, benefits and challenges. From 1,725 initial records, 15 peer-reviewed studies ,lastly from Indonesia and a few from Malaysia met the inclusion criteria. Findings show that Canva is widely used for visual learning and content creation in language, social studies and science subjects. It enhances student motivation, comprehension, creativity, improves writing and digital literacy. However, its classroom use remains short-term and teacher-centered , with limited focus on science and higher-order thinking. Reported challenges include low digital literacy, poor infrastructure and insufficient teacher training. Overall, Canva is a flexible platform that supports 21st-century learning, but equitable access and teacher readiness are essential for its effective technology integration.

title: Energy Economics Review: Advancing Knowledge at the Nexus of Energy Economy and Sustainability
abstract: The accelerating transformation of global energy systems presents complex challenges and opportunities for economies, institutions, and societies. This editorial introduces the Energy Economics Review (EER) as an interdisciplinary platform dedicated to advancing rigorous and policy-relevant research at the intersection of energy economics, environmental sustainability, and climate policy. It highlights the critical need for integrated analytical frameworks that capture the dynamic interplay between energy markets, technological innovation, financial systems, and governance structures. The editorial outlines the journal’s core thematic priorities, including energy transition strategies, renewable energy finance, market design and regulation, climate economics, and energy equity. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of sustainable finance, digitalisation, and institutional capacity in shaping low-carbon development pathways. The discussion further underscores the importance of methodological rigour, encouraging contributions employing advanced econometric techniques, system modelling, and comparative policy analysis. By fostering global inclusivity and interdisciplinary dialogue, EER aims to bridge the gap between academic research and policy implementation. The editorial concludes by positioning the journal as a critical forum for generating evidence-based insights that support economically viable, environmentally sustainable, and socially equitable energy systems in both developed and developing contexts.

title: <b>Fully Analogue Approach to Signal Encryption with Chua’s Circuit </b><b></b>
abstract: This project proposes an approach to utilizing Chua’s circuit to create an encryption method using passive and active analogue components. Chua’s circuit is a nonlinear oscillator that produces a chaotic output theorized by Leon Chua in 1983. This circuit can be coupled with a sister circuit to produce synchronized signals. Due to the chaotic output, there have been several designs proposed and developed for using this circuit for encryption. Using the Antoniou Gyrator method of creating an equivalent inductance, and the common Op-Amp equivalent for Chua’s diode, it is possible to create 3 Chua circuits for the encryption and decryption aspects for a total of 6. With these, a looped periodic analogue control signal can be added. Then the signal can be encrypted with predetermined weights to specified X, Y, and Z outputs of the circuit, and sum up this solution. From there, the user potentiometers to input the weights for the unknown values. The user will also be selecting an X, Y, or Z output for each circuit. This gives us a mechanism, similar to a combination lock, in which can only be found by the specific control signal from knowing the weights that the potentiometers must be set to. This work does not aim to replace modern digital cryptography but rather explores analog-domain signal obfuscation and secure masking techniques. This design can be useful for specific analogue-based encryption, with a focus on audible sound.

title: Digital Transformation Strategies for UAE Startups in the AI Era: A Critical Literature Review and Qualitative Research Framework
abstract: This article presents a comprehensive examination of digital transformation strategies for UAE startups navigating the artificial intelligence era, synthesizing insights from 163 scholarly sources and proposing a qualitative research framework based on 15 senior leadership interviews. The critical literature review reveals that successful digital transformation in UAE startups requires the strategic integration of three interdependent pillars: digital leadership capabilities, AI adoption practices, and organizational readiness. Key findings indicate that UAE startups face distinct challenges including skills shortages, ethical governance concerns, and resource constraints, while benefiting from supportive government initiatives aligned with national smart transformation agendas. The proposed qualitative methodology employs semi-structured interviews with 15 senior leaders across UAE startup ecosystems to capture nuanced insights into strategic decision-making, implementation challenges, and success factors. This research contributes to both academic understanding and practical guidance for startup leaders, policymakers, and ecosystem stakeholders seeking to accelerate digital transformation in the UAE's dynamic entrepreneurial landscape.

title: Development of Decision-Making Tools for Regulating Heavy Vehicle Passage on Embankment Dams
abstract: Abstract Embankment dams are frequently located in areas with specialized transportation needs, such as mining or heavy equipment transport. In remote northern regions with limited road infrastructure, utilizing dam crests for heavy vehicle circulation can significantly reduce travel times and costs, offering economic and environmental benefits such as lower fuel consumption and the avoidance of bridge construction. It is critical to establish appropriate tolerance criteria to ensure safe vehicle loads on the dam crest. The present study proposes a decision-making framework to regulate heavy vehicle passage across embankment dams based on permanent deformation and plastic strain rate criteria in the dam's core. The methodology was developed using field instrumentation data from three embankment dams to define representative modeling parameters. The proposed approach is then applied to a fourth embankment dam through a working example to demonstrate its practical implementation. The results show that the framework enables dam owners and operators to identify allowable vehicle loads and traffic scenarios within acceptable deformation limits, providing a practical decision-support framework that can be adapted to other embankment dams with site-specific inputs and engineering judgment.

title: Fluorine-Doped Cesium Tungsten Bronze-Integrated Thermally Responsive Poly( N -isopropylacrylamide- co -acrylamide)-Based Copolymeric Smart Hydrogel Films for NIR Shielding
abstract: Abstract Developing advanced materials and composites to counter the global energy crisis arising from climate change is one of the crucial research areas nowadays. In this context, the present research reports the successful fabrication of a high-performance thermoresponsive hydrogel film for thermochromic light regulation and solar NIR shielding applications. Poly(N-isopropylacrylamide-co-acrylamide) (PNAM) copolymeric hydrogels integrated with a biobased acrylated epoxide methyl ricinoleate (AEMR) monomer are prepared through free radical polymerization with a tunable lower critical solution temperature (LCST) in the range of 35−40 °C. The dark blue-colored fluorine (F−)-doped cesium tungsten bronze Cs0.33WO3−xFx (FCWO) nanoparticles are synthesized via a facile hydrothermal route to enhance the near-IR (NIR) blocking capacity of the films. The optimized composite hydrogel film (PNAM-FCWO-0.3 film with 0.37 mm thickness) displayed a visible light transmittance (Tlum) of ∼70.03%, a remarkable solar modulation (ΔTsol) of ∼67.99%, and high NIR shielding of ∼89%. Moreover, the optimized composite hydrogel film (PNAM-FCWO-0.3) decreased the internal temperature of the model house by ∼10.8 °C compared to the standard glass window-based identical model house. With its excellent flexibility, water stability, and heat absorption capacity, the PNAM-FCWO composite films show significant potential for fabricating smart hydrogel films for NIR shielding and energy saving applications.

title: Polymeric nanocomposites for eco-friendly and industrial applications: a comprehensive review
abstract: Abstract Polymeric nanocomposites (PNCs) are formed by dispersing fillers with at least one dimension in the 1–100 nm range in a polymer matrix, and the resulting materials often outperform either constituent alone. Because the interfacial area per unit volume scales inversely with the smallest filler dimension, a few volumes per cent of well-dispersed nanofiller can alter the mechanical, electrical, optical, magnetic and gas-barrier properties of the host polymer, at loadings substantially lower than those required with conventional micro-scale fillers. These benefits have attracted increasing attention from sectors such as water treatment, flexible electronics, aerospace shielding and food preservation. This review provides a thematically organised and critical overview of the PNC field. It first sets out the structure–property fundamentals (interfacial area, interphase volume, filler aspect ratio and dispersion state) that link nanoscale structure to macroscopic performance. It then compares four established fabrication routes (melt blending, in situ polymerisation, solution mixing and electrospinning) in terms of dispersion quality, interfacial bonding, scalability and environmental burden. Smart PNCs that respond to heat, light, electric and magnetic fields are compared with respect to mechanism, representative systems, advantages and limitations. The application sections compile quantitative data on dye and heavy-metal removal, sensing performance (detection limits and linear ranges), electromagnetic interference shielding effectiveness and shelf-life extension, and discuss safety, migration and regulatory requirements for food-contact and biomedical uses together with life-cycle considerations. Finally, the review identifies persistent bottlenecks (filler agglomeration, cost, reproducibility, toxicological uncertainty and regulatory gaps) and sets out research priorities, including scale-up, long-term durability, standardised testing and techno-economic assessment, that could accelerate responsible commercialisation.

title: X-ray Crystallography of a Nanobody/JAM-1 Complex Informs Barrier Weakening and Enhanced Drug Permeability in a Cellular Blood–Brain Barrier Model
abstract: Abstract For pharmacological treatments of brain disorders, the blood–brain barrier (BBB) poses a formidable obstacle, tightly restricting the cerebral uptake of therapeutic agents. Tight junction (TJ) binders, including peptides, proteins, and monoclonal antibodies, that specifically bind to the extracellular domains (ECDs) of TJ proteins are increasingly being explored as BBB-weakening agents for enhanced drug delivery to the brain. Given that nanobodies (Nbs) can access epitopes that are often inaccessible to conventional antibodies, we obtained 16 Nbs with unique CDRs via immunization of alpaca with the ECD of either human (h) or murine JAM-1 (mJAM-1), a major TJ protein. Twelve Nb candidates exhibited high-affinity binding to mJAM-1, as measured by surface plasmon resonance (SPR), and these interactions were further validated for 9 Nbs by immunostaining of JAM-1-overexpressing cells. Five Nbs were found to weaken the barrier of the eGFP-hCldn5-MDCKII cellular monolayer, as shown by reduced transendothelial electrical resistance (TEER). X-ray crystallography revealed that the lead barrier-weakening Nb, E6, binds to the membrane-proximal nondimeric D2 domain of mJAM-1. Mutating key residues at this interface eliminated the BBB-weakening effect of E6, as evidenced by unaltered sodium fluorescence (NaFI) leakage in both eGFP-hCldn5-MDCKII and mJAM1-mGL-MDCKII cellular monolayers compared with the nontreated control. Our study highlights the potential of JAM-1-targeting Nbs as BBB modulators, offering a promising approach for generating TJ binders to enhance brain drug delivery.

title: Ultrastable de novo SuperMyo proteins enable high-performance macroscopic fibers from minimal repeats
abstract: Conventional routes to strong protein fibers rely on the assembly of high-molecular-weight polymers, where mechanical performance is achieved by increasing the number of tandem repeats within the polypeptide chain. This repeat-number strategy inherently complicates production and limits scalability. Here, we introduce a contrasting paradigm in which macroscopic strength is derived not from chain length, but from the increased intrinsic mechanostability of each repeating unit. We implement this using computationally designed immunoglobulin-domain-based SuperMyo proteins, whose force-bearing β-strands are engineered to form ultra-dense hydrogen-bond networks, yielding unfolding forces nearly double those of natural immunoglobulin domains at a pulling speed of 1000 nm s−1. When assembled into minimal tetrameric constructs (only four repeats), these designed units retain their high nanomechanical stability. Processed via wet-spinning, the tetramers form continuous macroscopic fibers with a tensile strength up to 372 MPa and a toughness of 61 MJ m⁻³. Crucially, this performance matches or exceeds that of previously reported fibers spun from polymers containing far more repeats (e.g., 64-mers). Structural analyses confirm that the enhanced stability of the monomers promotes superior β-sheet crystallization and alignment during fiber formation. By demonstrating that engineering the mechanical stability of protein building blocks is a potential strategy for producing strong protein fibers from low-repeat-number constructs, this work establishes a more efficient and scalable foundation for manufacturing high-performance protein-based materials. High-performance biofuels require a well-defined flash point, yet the coexistence of pentanol isomers can introduce ignition-point variations that compromise fuel performance. Here, the authors present an electrochemiluminescence shunt strategy based on a bifunctional catalytic system that exploits the distinct reactive oxygen species scavenging properties of pentanol isomers. The approach generates differential anodic and cathodic luminol signals, enabling their precise discrimination and providing a powerful tool for fuel-quality assessment

title: Efficient Degradation and Recycling of Waste Formaldehyde Polymers to Value‐Added Diindolylmethane Compounds
abstract: ABSTRACT The effective degradation of formaldehyde polymers catalyzed by Y(OTf) 3 with indole derivatives in water has been achieved, yielding a series of diindolylmethane compounds with added value. It provides a new route with additional potential for the upcycling of waste paraformaldehyde and polyoxymethylene plastic as a green alternative C1 synthon.

title: Composite Microgels with Dynamically Switchable Stiffness
abstract: Whereas macroscopic hydrogels with precisely controllable and dynamically adjustable properties do exist, the development of similar platforms at the microscale is much more challenging. Here, we introduce a novel composite microgel system comprising the two cytocompatible biopolymers alginate and mucin, which are functionalized to simultaneously enable covalent and ionic cross-linking. As a consequence, the initial stiffness of the generated microgels can not only be tailored over a range from ∼350 Pa to ∼7 kPa, but it is also possible to first increase and then decrease the microgel stiffness on demand at any time point post-production. Owing to the two distinct biopolymer components in the microgels, they can be enzymatically degraded and resist biofouling events by bacteria. With this set of properties, this microgel system should be highly suitable for versatile applications in bioengineering or mechanobiology.

title: Structure–Property Relationships in Flexible PVA /Polypyrrole Films: Optical and Dielectric Spectroscopy for Optoelectronic and Energy‐Storage Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Polyvinyl alcohol/polypyrrole (PVA/PPy) blend films with varying PPy loadings (0, 1, 3, and 5 wt%) were produced via solution‐casting method. The impact of PPy inclusion on structural, optical, dielectric, and electrical properties of fabricated films was examined. Structural investigations showed that PPy interacted successfully with the PVA matrix, reducing crystallinity and forming robust interfacial contacts (corroborated by FTIR and XRD). PPy was uniformly distributed inside hosting matrix, forming conductive channels at higher loading. Optical investigations revealed a notable increase in absorbance, a reduction in the direct optical bandgap (from 5.25 to 4.85 eV) and an increase in Urbach energy (from 1.67 to 2.40 eV), indicating enhanced localized states and structural disorder. Dielectric studies showed an increase in dielectric constant with increasing PPy content (from 1.98 to 10.9), accompanied by improved interfacial polarization and charge‐storage capacity. Analysis of electrical modulus and impedance confirmed accelerated relaxation dynamics and decreased bulk resistance (from 3.8 × 10 10 to 0.9 × 10 10 Ω), accompanied by enhanced charge transport. AC conductivity and discharged energy density increased significantly with PPy loading (from ∼8.8 × 10 −6 to 4.80 × 10 −5 J m −3 ). The results indicate that incorporating PPy effectively modifies PVA' properties, supporting its use in optoelectronics and energy‐storage systems.

title: Sustainable recovery of active compounds from coffee husks using enzymatic aqueous extraction
abstract: Abstract This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of aqueous extraction combined with the use of the enzyme Viscozyme ® L for the recovery of compounds from coffee husks. Therefore, initially, extractions were conducted to determine the condition for maximum extraction of total phenolic acids (TPA), based on the effect of the variables enzyme concentration (1 wt% to 5 wt%), temperature (45 °C to 55 °C), and time (20 to 60 min). Subsequently, extractions were performed with and without enzyme at different times, obtaining the yield, composition, antimicrobial activity and cytotoxicity of the dry extract. Based on the results, maximum TPA extraction was observed at 45 °C, 60 min, and with 1 wt% of enzyme. The use of the enzyme (1wt%) in the extraction medium provided an increase in the yield of dry extract from 10 to 43% at the evaluated times (20 to 60 min), in addition to resulting in extracts with greater antioxidant potential and higher levels of phenolic compounds, when compared to aqueous extraction alone. The extract was composed by phenolic acids and kaempferol, being chlorogenic acid the most abundant compound. A high correlation was found between chlorogenic acid and antioxidant potential ( r = 0.98). The extract exhibited bacteriostatic activity, with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) ranging from 8.33 to 10.00 mg/mL. The application of the extract, at the tested concentrations (50 to 400 µg/mL), did not compromise the viability of HaCaT cells.

title: Recyclable Lignin‐Based Thermadapt Shape Memory Polymers With Near‐Infrared Light Response
abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) have been designed to address the recycling challenges associated with thermosets, while preserving their mechanical properties. However, producing biobased CANs with intelligent response capabilities remains challenging. We report the preparation of lignin‐polypentadecalactone‐based CANs with a high biomass content (86.2–96.4 wt%). In lignin‐PPDL CANs, acetoacetate‐modified lignin serves dual roles as the hard segment and crosslinker, while the polypentadecalactone (PPDL) soft segment exhibits a semi‐crystalline nature. Crosslinking between the soft PPDL and hard lignin segments is achieved via vinylogous urethane chemistry, resulting in CANs with markedly enhanced mechanical properties and recyclability. When applied to shape memory systems, the semi‐crystalline polymer domains act as reversible molecular switches, while dynamic bond exchange enables topological rearrangement, allowing reconfiguration of the permanent shape, characteristic of thermadapt shape memory polymers. Leveraging the photothermal conversion capability of lignin, we successfully developed near‐infrared (NIR) light‐responsive shape memory CANs. These innovative materials hold promising prospects for applications in intelligent materials, given their unique combination of mechanical strength, shape memory capabilities, and responsiveness to NIR light. Furthermore, the approach of tailoring the new material based on the specific properties of the raw material in this study offers a novel avenue for designing high‐performance multifunctional CANs.

title: Transient polymer nanocomposites with programmable functions for zero-residue and self-regulating food applications
abstract: The next generation of sustainable food materials must move beyond passive biodegradability toward systems that actively control their function, lifespan, and environmental fate. This review introduces the emerging concept of transient and programmable polymer nanocomposites, a transformative class of materials designed to perform specific food-related functions, adapt to changing conditions, and subsequently disassemble into benign, zero-residue products. Unlike conventional biodegradable nanocomposites that degrade through uncontrolled environmental processes, transient systems enable triggerable and time-defined disintegration, providing precise control over material persistence and nanoparticle release. Similarly, the ability to modify material properties in response to stimuli can be extended to include feedback-driven control of antimicrobial, barrier, or antioxidant properties. The review provides an integrated perspective of the interaction between nano-polymer, function, degradation, and lifecycle sustainability. New materials are reviewed that include sustainable polymer, transient degradation chemistry, nano-enabled sensing, self-regulating release systems, and intelligent packaging. Special attention is paid to balancing function with safety, as well as circular economy. The future directions for these materials are the use of artificial intelligence as a tool, closed-loop packaging, and permanently floating nanocomposites are also explored. Through the introduction of the term "function-response-disappearance", we are addressing a gap in the literature on food nanotechnology, while describing a roadmap for safe, adaptive and zero-waste materials that can aid resilient and sustainable food systems.

title: Mitochondrial complex IV disruption is a detrimental pathology conferring ssusceptibility to alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Mitochondrial complex IV (CIV) is an integral part of the mitochondrial electron transport chain (ETC) and plays a pivotal role in maintaining mitochondrial function. In contrast to the long-standing recognition of its dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease (AD), the exact role of CIV deficit in the pathogenesis of this neurodegenerative disorder remains poorly defined. In this study, by incorporating clinical resources, mouse- and human-based models of AD risk, and a genetic approach to bypass defective CIV via the ectopic expression of alternative oxidase (AOX), we examined whether CIV deficits are a pathogenic driver of or a beneficial adaptation to AD-associated pathologies. Our results showed a clinicopathological association between neuronal CIV dysfunction and pathological characteristics of AD. Further experiments linked defective CIV to the development of mitochondrial dysfunction and synaptic loss in the tested mouse- and human-based models of AD risk. In addition, a reciprocal relationship between CIV dysfunction and amyloid pathology was determined. Lastly, a proteome-wide association study (PWAS) using genetic data from large-scale AD cohorts identified that downregulation of COX11, a crucial CIV assembly factor, confers susceptibility to AD risk. Collectively, our findings suggest that CIV dysfunction is a detrimental pathology contributing to AD-associated mitochondrial and neuronal damage. The dual role of CIV dysfunction, both as a consequence of and a contributor to amyloid toxicity in AD pathogenesis, further justifies the therapeutic potential of strategies targeting CIV deficits to diversify the tools for prevention and treatment of this neurodegenerative disorder.

title: IDPForge: deep learning of proteins with global and local regions of disorder
abstract: Abstract Although machine learning has transformed protein structure prediction of folded protein ground states with remarkable accuracy, intrinsically disordered proteins and regions (IDPs/IDRs) are defined by diverse and dynamical structural ensembles that are predicted with low confidence by algorithms such as AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold. We present a machine learning method, IDPForge ( I ntrinsically D isordered P rotein, FO lded and disordered R egion GE nerator), that exploits a transformer protein language diffusion model to create all-atom IDP ensembles and IDR ensembles that maintains the folded domains. IDPForge does not require sequence-specific training, back transformations from coarse-grained representations, nor ensemble reweighting. The created IDP/IDR conformational ensembles show good agreement with both NMR and SAXS solution experimental data, and options for biasing with experimental restraints are available if desired. IDPForge with these diverse capabilities facilitates integrative and structural studies for proteins that contain intrinsic disorder, and is available as an open source resource for general use.

title: Supercritical Fluid‐Based Synthesis of Nanomaterials for Energy Storage Applications: A Pathway Toward High‐Entropy Oxides
abstract: ABSTRACT Supercritical fluid processing has developed into a versatile and environmentally responsible approach for the controlled fabrication of nanomaterials, distinguished by low density, viscosity, high diffusivity, and negligible surface tension. These intrinsic features enhance nucleation, efficient mass transport, and accurate control over particle dimensions, morphology, and compositional uniformity. This review comprehensively examines the fundamental principles of supercritical fluids, encompassing phase behavior, thermophysical characteristics, and the mechanisms governing nanoparticle formation, along with important engineering aspects related to both batch and continuous‐flow reactor configurations. The preparation of metal, metal oxide, and composite nanostructures through supercritical techniques is critically evaluated, emphasizing their benefits compared with traditional solid‐state and solution‐based synthesis routes. Special attention is given to the evolution toward high‐entropy oxides, where supercritical conditions enable homogeneous multication distribution, enhanced phase development, and defect modulation under kinetically advantageous environments. By establishing clear relationships between processing conditions, structural characteristics, and electrochemical performance, this review highlights the promise of SCF‐enabled methodologies as scalable and sustainable pathways for designing advanced multicomponent oxide materials suited for energy storage and catalytic applications.

title: Scalable Upcycling of Industrial Waste Polytetrafluoroethylene Into Porous Carbon Nanosheets by Zeolite Particle Templates for Capacitive Energy Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Upcycling highly stable polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) waste into value‐added carbon materials is fundamentally hindered by its complete zero‐residue pyrolysis, which exclusively emits hazardous fluorocarbons rather than forming solid carbon frameworks. Herein, we present a scalable zeolite‐particle‐templated cocarbonization strategy that catalytically transforms industrial PTFE waste into hierarchical porous carbon nanosheets (PCNs) while fixing over 81% of the fluorine as recyclable NaF. Comprehensive mechanistic investigations reveal that the ZSM‐5 template electronically activates C─F bonds and lowers the defluorination barrier, driving a successive‐condensation structural evolution. The resulting PCN, featuring an ultrahigh specific surface area and hierarchical porosity, delivers exceptional dual‐mode energy storage performances. In supercapacitors, PCNs achieve a remarkable specific capacitance of 429.6 F g −1 and outstanding rate capabilities driven by reversible pseudocapacitance and ion coadsorption. Concurrently, in carbon‐based aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (CAZBs), the PCNs deliver a high specific capacity of 267.0 mAh g −1 with robust extreme‐temperature adaptability (−25°C). Validated by a continuous industrial‐scale piping and instrumentation design (PID), this strategy demonstrates high commercial viability with low energy storage costs, pioneering a waste‐to‐wealth strategy for advanced carbon materials for energy storage.

title: Natural Polymer-Based Microspheres For Anti-Inflammatory Drug Delivery : Materials, Characterization, and Therapeutic Applications
abstract: Microsphere-based drug delivery systems have gained considerable attention in pharmaceutical research due to their ability to provide controlled, targeted, and sustained release of therapeutic agents while minimizing systemic side effects. In particular, microspheres formulated from natural polymers such as chitosan, sodium alginate, pectin, and gelatin have emerged as promising carriers for anti-inflammatory therapy owing to their biocompatibility, biodegradability, low toxicity, and responsiveness to physiological stimuli. This review comprehensively discusses the role of natural polymer–based microspheres in inflammatory drug delivery, focusing on polymer characteristics, preparation methods, release and delivery mechanisms, and routes of administration. Emphasis is placed on their application in both in vitro and in vivo anti-inflammatory models, including carrageenan-induced paw edema, lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammation, and monosodium iodoacetate–induced osteoarthritis. Evidence from preclinical studies demonstrates that these systems are capable of enhancing drug stability, prolonging residence time at the inflamed site, modulating inflammatory mediators such as TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, and improving overall therapeutic efficacy compared with free drugs. Despite these advantages, challenges related to polymer variability, mechanical stability, release precision, and large-scale production remain. Future advancements in polymer modification, hybrid polymer systems, and advanced fabrication technologies are expected to further optimize natural polymer-based microspheres, supporting their potential application in personalized and long-term inflammatory therapy.

title: Carbon‐Supported Catalytic Systems Assembled by π–π Interactions
abstract: The immobilization of molecular catalysts on carbonaceous supports through noncovalent π–π interactions has emerged as an attractive strategy for developing more sustainable catalytic processes. Carbon‐based materials combine high surface areas, chemical and thermal stability, and tunable surface properties, while enabling the reversible immobilization of π‐conjugated catalysts, notably through pyrene–surface interactions. This approach offers potential advantages in catalyst recovery, recycling, product purification, and, in the case of metal complexes, the reduction of metal contamination. Moreover, the proximity of immobilized catalytic species may provide opportunities for cooperative or tandem catalytic processes. This review surveys the use of carbonaceous allotropes—including graphene, reduced graphene oxide, carbon nanotubes, fullerenes, carbon black, charcoal, and magnetic carbon‐based materials—as supports for organometallic and organic catalysts. Particular attention is devoted to their applications in achiral and enantioselective transformations, catalyst stability and recyclability, and, where available, comparisons with the corresponding homogeneous systems. The influence of support characteristics, including material quality, aggregation state, dispersion, and purification, is also considered as a critical factor affecting catalytic performance and the comparability of reported results. By bringing together these developments, this review highlights the opportunities and current limitations of noncovalent catalyst immobilization on carbonaceous supports for sustainable organic synthesis.

title: MTRF1 reverses cisplatin resistance in bladder cancer by competitively disrupting OTUB1-mediated deubiquitination of SLC25A5 to trigger ferroptosis
abstract: Abstract Cisplatin (DDP)-based chemotherapy remains a standard treatment for advanced bladder cancer, yet acquired resistance remains a major cause of therapeutic failure. Here, we identify mitochondrial translation release factor 1 (MTRF1) as a critical suppressor of cisplatin resistance and a regulator of ferroptotic vulnerability in bladder cancer. MTRF1 was markedly downregulated in bladder cancer tissues and was further reduced in cisplatin-resistant clinical specimens as well as in T24-DDP and 5637-DDP resistant cell models. Restoration of MTRF1 significantly resensitized resistant cells to cisplatin, decreased IC50 values, and suppressed proliferation, colony formation, migration, and survival. Mechanistically, MTRF1 promoted a ferroptosis-prone state, as evidenced by elevated intracellular iron and malondialdehyde, increased Acyl-CoA Synthetase Long Chain Family Member 4 (ACSL4), reduced Glutathione Peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and Solute Carrier Family 7 Member 11 (SLC7A11), and enhanced sensitivity to Erastin. MTRF1 also triggered mitochondrial membrane depolarization, reactive oxygen species accumulation, oxidative redox shift, a reduced GSH/GSSG ratio, and inhibition of the Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant program, indicating a profound collapse of mitochondrial and redox homeostasis. At the molecular level, MTRF1 physically interacted with Solute Carrier Family 25 Member 5 (SLC25A5) and antagonized its pro-survival function. Further analyses demonstrated that MTRF1 promoted ubiquitin-proteasome-mediated degradation of SLC25A5 by increasing its polyubiquitination and competitively displacing the deubiquitinase OTUB1. In vivo, MTRF1 restoration enhanced cisplatin responsiveness in xenograft models, whereas deferoxamine partially reversed the antitumor effect, supporting a partial contribution of ferroptosis to this response. Collectively, these findings establish MTRF1 as a key determinant of cisplatin sensitivity in bladder cancer and uncover an MTRF1-OTUB1-SLC25A5 axis that links mitochondrial proteostasis to oxidative stress and ferroptotic cell death. Targeting this pathway may represent a promising strategy for overcoming cisplatin resistance in bladder cancer.

title: Selective Monovalent Cation Transport in Two‐Dimensional Polymer Membranes via Charge Control of Nanochannels
abstract: ABSTRACT Monovalent cations like Li + , Na + , and K + are now regarded as important components for advanced electrochemical energy storage technologies for achieving high energy density and power density. However, due to their identical charge number and similar hydration diameter, the low separation efficiency of monovalent cations during their recovery and use presents a major bottleneck for the rapidly sustainable energy development. Herein, we propose a charge‐engineering strategy for efficiently tuning the cation‐channel interaction via varying the membrane charges toward rapid and selective transmembrane transport of monovalent Li + and K + cations. In this respect, we develop charged polyketoenamine‐based two‐dimensional polymer membranes (2DPMs) at liquid–liquid interface, which feature high crystallinity with pH‐responsive quasi‐1D porous channels functionalized by acyl oxime groups. Notably, the positively charged 2D polyketoenamine simultaneously exhibits ultrahigh K + permeation rate (361.7 mmol·m −2 ·h −1 ) and high K + /Li + selectivity (6.6), as well as a record‐high K + diffusion coefficient (2.9 × 10 −10 m 2 ·s −1 ), which are superior to the state‐of‐the‐art graphene‐ and polymer‐based membranes (< 1.7 × 10 −10 m 2 ·s −1 ) as well as neutral and negatively charged 2D polyketoenamine membranes.

title: Response Surface Optimization of Acidification Parameters and Solvent Recyclability for Deep Eutectic Solvent (DES)-Based Depolymerization of Polyethylene Terephthalate
abstract: In the context of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) depolymerization, growing attention has been directed toward the use of alternative capable of functioning as both solvent and catalyst. These dual-function systems offer notable advantages, including reduced energy requirements, simplified processing, and enhanced sustainability. From a process optimization perspective, three key stages govern overall energy and material efficiency: (i) PET depolymerization, (ii) the subsequent acidification step for the recovery of terephthalic acid (TPA), and (iii) solvent recovery for reuse in subsequent depolymerization cycles. The depolymerization step has been widely studied, however, the latter two stages remain underexplored. To enhance process sustainability, the acidification stage was optimized by minimizing acid and water consumption while maintaining high product quality. A Box– Behnken Design (BBD) within the framework of Response Surface Methodology (RSM) was employed to optimize key parameters, including acid volume, acid concentration, and water content for dilution. Model predictions using tetrabutylammonium bromide and sulfolane-based DES suggested that 13 mL of water, 2.5 mL of HCl, and 36 wt% acid concentration would yield 79.7% TPA, while laboratory validation achieved 83.0%, corresponding to a mean error of 4.1%. In terms of solvent recovery, the DES was successfully reused for up to three consecutive cycles without significant structural degradation or loss of solvolytic performance. The recovered TPA is a high-value monomer with broad market potential, and Fourier Transform Infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy analysis confirms its quality as comparable to that of virgin material. This enhances its appeal for supporting a circular and sustainable plastics economy.

title: Poly Schiff bases embedded polyrotaxane for flexible memristor and artificial synapses
abstract: Abstract Poly Schiff bases (PSBs) with tunable conductivity by reversible protonation and deprotonation, are promising memristive materials to mimic ion‐mediated signaling in biological synaptic transmission. However, most PSBs suffer from poor solubility and processability due to the rigid backbones, limiting the fabrication and performance of memristors. Herein, solution‐processable PSB was designed and synthesized by threading the conjugated chain through cyclodextrin macrocycles. The resulting PSB embedded polyrotaxanes based memristors exhibit excellent environmental stability (>8 months) and durability, high ON/OFF ratio (10 7 ), and high‐speed switching (25 ns) with fully addressed resistive switching mechanism. Moreover, the devices demonstrate remarkable mechanical flexibility, and the performance maintains even after 100 bending cycles at a curvature radius of 3 mm. Furthermore, synaptic behaviors such as short‐term, long‐term and spike‐timing‐dependent plasticity were emulated. The memristor was also implemented for image recognition, showing promising potential for neuromorphic computing. This work provides a new strategy to improve the solubility of PSB for flexible and wearable electronics.

title: Improving the Sensitivity in Chiral Analysis by Capillary Electrophoresis
abstract: Chiral analysis plays a relevant role in numerous scientific fields, such as the pharmaceutical, biomedical, agrochemical, environmental, or food science, due to the different properties that stereoisomers may present. Capillary electrophoresis (CE) techniques, mainly electrokinetic chromatography (EKC) and micellar electrokinetic chromatography (MEKC), are well-established techniques to achieve enantiomeric separations owing to its high selectivity, methodological versatility, and low consumption of reagents and samples. In this context, method sensitivity is a critical characteristic, as it determines the capability to detect and quantify enantiomers at trace levels and to assess the enantiomeric purity of raw materials, pharmaceutical or agrochemical formulations, and food ingredients, among others. This article reviews the analytical strategies reported from 2022 to June 2026 aimed at enhancing the sensitivity in chiral CE techniques and to apply them to the analysis of pharmaceutical formulations, and to biological, environmental, and food samples. Off-line and in-capillary preconcentration strategies, as well as their combinations, together with the use of alternative detections systems to UV-Vis detection, are described as the most effective. The most relevant results are presented and critically discussed through the manuscript.

title: Metal–Organic Frameworks for Sustainable Photocatalytic and Electrocatalytic HMF‐to‐FDCA Conversion: From Catalyst Engineering to Energy‐Saving Paired Electrolysis Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic and electrocatalytic upgrading of lignocellulosic biomass into value‐added chemicals offers a sustainable route to carbon neutrality. 5‑hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) is a key intermediate because its selective oxidation yields 2,5‑furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA), a renewable monomer for biodegradable polyesters. This review summarizes metal–organic frameworks (MOFs)‐based catalysts for photo‐ and electrochemical HMF oxidation, covering pristine MOFs and MOF‐derived catalytic systems. This review further discusses key modification strategies, including dynamic structural regulation, multi‐active‐site design, and derivative structural optimization. Through these strategies, MOF‐based systems modulate electronic structure, active‐site accessibility, and mass/charge transport, thereby enhancing the activity and FDCA selectivity of photocatalytic and electrocatalytic HMF oxidation. Building on this mechanistic understanding, we examine the structure–activity relationships and reaction mechanisms revealed by in situ characterizations and density functional theory calculations. This review also assesses paired electrolysis systems that integrate anodic HMFOR with cathodic hydrogen evolution or other value‐added reductions. Finally, persistent challenges such as scalable synthesis and reactor design are addressed, along with future perspectives for rational catalyst design and industrial implementation of MOF‐based biomass upgrading.

title: Constitutive Modeling of Degradation‐Induced Mechanical Behavior in Commercial Polydioxanone for Implantable Devices
abstract: In this study, the mechanical behavior of a commercially available polydioxanone (RESOMER X 206S, Evonik) and its evolution under in vitro degradation were investigated through combined experimental and constitutive modeling approaches. Tensile tests were performed on injection-molded dog-bone specimens at multiple time points during immersion in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) at 37°C for up to 4 weeks. Experimentally, the material exhibited a distinct transition from ductile to brittle behavior after approximately 3 weeks of degradation. Based on these findings, an extension of the Three Network Model (TNM), termed TNM for Degradation (TNMfD), was developed and validated to predict the degradation-dependent mechanical response of biodegradable polymers under nearly incompressible conditions. The model parameters of the TNM were initially identified to accurately reproduce the mechanical response of PDO before degradation, establishing baseline values for degradation-insensitive parameters and reference points for degradation-dependent ones. Subsequently, two formulations of the hydrolytic damage parameter were evaluated within the TNMfD framework. Both formulations successfully captured the degradation-induced changes in mechanical behavior, demonstrating good agreement with experimental data. The proposed TNMfD provides a robust, efficient numerical tool for the in silico assessment and design of biodegradable polymer-based medical devices.

title: Position‐Resolved Fluorescence Polarization Maps Segmental Rigidity in Block Copolymer Micelles in Aqueous and Biological Media
abstract: Polymeric micelles are widely used as nanoscale compartments for delivery, sensing, and soft-matter applications, yet their performance is governed not only by size and morphology but also by the local mobility of polymer segments within the assembly. Here, we describe a position-resolved fluorescence polarization strategy to map apparent segmental rigidity within block copolymer micelles. By covalently installing the same dansyl fluorophore at defined positions along an amphiphilic block copolymer chain, we selectively label the hydrophobic core, core-corona interface, and oligo(ethylene glycol) (OEG)-rich corona of the micelles. The resulting fluorescence polarization profiles reveal a pronounced core-to-corona apparent rigidity gradient in water, distinguish block-segregated micelles from compositionally matched random copolymer assemblies, and report micellar responses to temperature, cosolvent, and salt. This method further enables structural interrogation of polymer micelles in biologically relevant media, revealing the unexpected finding that biological serum exerts opposing effects on apparent chain rigidity in the micellar core and corona. Together, these results establish position-resolved fluorescence polarization as a practical platform for linking block copolymer structure, self-assembly, local chain dynamics, and biological stability, opening new opportunities to rationally design micelles with environment-responsive mechanical properties.

title: Recyclable Synthetic Polymer Nanoparticles for Sustained Target Neutralization
abstract: Abstract Synthetic polymers have emerged as protein-affinity materials capable of binding and neutralizing biological targets through optimized functional monomer compositions. However, these materials are often implicitly treated as single-use systems, largely because they are assumed to be unavailable for further interaction after cellular internalization. The intracellular fate of such materials, including their potential rerelease and sustained functional activity, remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that synthetic polymer nanoparticles (NPs) can undergo cellular recycling while preserving their functional activity. Using N-isopropylacrylamide (NIPAm)-based polymer NPs as a proof-of-concept system, we investigated their cellular uptake, intracellular trafficking, and extracellular release. We evaluated their functional performance using melittin as a model target. A fraction of internalized NPs was rereleased in a cell-type-dependent manner, with transient colocalization with Rab11 suggesting the possible involvement of recycling-associated pathways. Importantly, the released NPs retained their ability to bind and neutralize melittin, even after prior interaction with the target toxin, and remained functionally competent for subsequent binding events. Moreover, the NPs appeared to maintain their association with melittin during intracellular processing, indicating that their functional integrity is preserved throughout the recycling process. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that synthetic polymer NPs can function as reusable systems with extended functional lifetimes, thereby challenging the conventional single-use paradigm. This study provides a foundation for the design of next-generation nanomaterials with enhanced functional durability in biological environments.

title: Exploratory profiling of Rhizophora apiculata root-associated fungi and preliminary polycaprolactone surface modification assessed using amplicon sequencing and culture-based approaches
abstract: Microplastics are persistent environmental contaminants, and fungi associated with mangrove roots may offer a source of isolates for studying interactions with polymeric materials.This exploratory study profiled fungal DNA in a single pooled sample of Rhizophora apiculata roots using ITS amplicon sequencing and examined the FTIR spectra of polycaprolactone (PCL) samples following exposure to five cultured fungal isolates, designated fungal isolates S2-S6.Amplicon sequencing detected 48 fungal taxa, predominantly assigned to Ascomycota, with Aspergillus as the most abundant genus.The diversity indices suggested moderate diversity and relatively low dominance within the pooled sample.FTIR analysis revealed differences in PCL associated spectral features following exposure to the isolates, while principal component analysis (PCA) showed preliminary spectral differentiation among the analyzed samples.These observations indicate differences in the chemical or surface associated characteristics of the tested PCL samples; they do not demonstrate polymer mass loss, depolymerization, assimilation, or mineralization.The sequencing results represent fungal DNA detected in one pooled biological sample and do not establish the viability or endophytic status of the detected taxa.A correspondence between the cultured isolates and the detected amplicon sequence variants was not established.Quantitative mass-loss measurements, molecular weight and degradation product analyses, and experiments with appropriate controls and biological replication are needed to determine the nature and cause of the observed PCL associated spectral changes.

title: Hydrogel Microwells with Light‐Controlled Reversible Closure
abstract: ABSTRACT We present a light‐responsive hydrogel nanocomposite engineered into arrays of micrometer‐scale wells that can be selectively and sequentially closed and re‐opened via laser illumination. Polarization‐controlled light exposure induces anisotropic surface deformations, leading to the formation of protrusive flaps sealing the wells. Owing to the intrinsic elasticity and anti‐adhesive properties of the hydrogel matrix, the deformation process is partially reversible, allowing flap retraction and restoration of the original well geometry. This platform facilitates contactless, on‐demand trapping and release of microscale objects using a standard optical microscopy configuration. As a proof of concept, we demonstrate the controlled manipulation of a single polystyrene microbead using optical tweezers, including bead positioning within a well, light‐triggered closure, and subsequent reopening to release the particle into the surrounding aqueous environment.
