title: Modulating Electronic Structure and Morphology in Nb‐NiCoS for PET Plastic Upcycling
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic polyethylene terephthalate (PET) upcycling coupled with green hydrogen production offers an energy‐efficient route for plastic waste valorization. Herein, Nb‐incorporated NiCoS electrocatalysts are synthesized on nickel foam via a one‐step chemical bath deposition route for PET electro‐upcycling. Nb incorporation modulates the electronic structure and morphology of NiCoS, producing defect‐rich vertically interconnected nanosheets with abundant electrochemically dynamic Ni 3+ /Co 3+ active sites. The optimized electronic structure promotes reconstruction into active NiOOH/CoOOH species, resulting in enhanced performance toward the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), oxygen evolution reaction (OER), ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR), and PET hydrolysate oxidation reaction (POR). Nb‐NiCoS requires 1.32 and 1.34 V vs RHE to achieve 100 mA cm −2 for EGOR and POR, respectively, significantly lower than OER (1.52 V vs RHE). Mechanistic analysis reveals an indirect oxy‐hydroxide‐mediated oxidation pathway, enabling selective conversion of PET‐derived EG into formic acid with a Faradaic efficiency of 93.3% (with ~100% selectivity) and a production rate of 1.16 mmol h −1 cm −2 at 100 mA cm −2 . Coupling PET electro‐upcycling with hydrogen production reduces the energy consumption to 3.52 kWh Nm −3 from 4.49 kWh Nm −3 for conventional water electrolysis, enabling energy saving of 21.3%, highlighting a scalable strategy for simultaneous plastic waste valorization and hydrogen production.

title: Translucency and Masking Ability of CAD / CAM Milled Denture Base Resins of Different Shades and Thicknesses Against Metal Substrates
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective To evaluate the translucency and masking ability of CAD/CAM milled denture base resins of different shades and thicknesses against gold‐ and silver‐colored metal substrates. Materials and Methods Two independent experiments were conducted using separate specimens. Circular specimens (Φ10 mm) were fabricated from five shades (P1–P5) of CAD/CAM milled denture base resin at thicknesses of 1, 2, 3, and 5 mm ( n = 8). For the 1‐, 2‐, and 3‐mm specimens, the color coordinates were measured against white and black backgrounds, as well as gold‐ and silver‐colored metal substrates. The 5‐mm specimens superimposed on the black background were defined as the baseline color reference for each shade. The translucency parameter (TP 00 ) was calculated based on measurements against white and black backgrounds, and the color difference (Δ E 00 ), which represents the masking ability of the respective specimen, was calculated by comparing measurements against the metal substrates with the corresponding baseline color reference. Analysis of variance was used for statistical analysis, and exploratory correlation analyses were used to assess the association between baseline color coordinates and Δ E 00 ( α = 0.05). Results Both TP 00 and Δ E 00 values significantly decreased with increasing thickness for all shades, and all thickness‐related ΔTP 00 values exceeded the translucency acceptability threshold (TAT = 2.62). For the gold‐colored metal substrate, the Δ E 00 values at 1 mm exceeded the acceptability threshold (AT = 2.8) for all shades. At 2 mm, the Δ E 00 values were below AT for the P1 and P3 shades but remained above AT for the other shades. At 3 mm, the Δ E 00 values were below AT but remained above the perceptibility threshold (PT = 1.1) for P1–P4, whereas P5 remained slightly above AT. For the silver‐colored metal substrate, the Δ E 00 values at 1 mm exceeded AT for all shades. At 2 mm, they were below AT but remained above PT for all shades, whereas at 3 mm, they were below PT for all shades except P2. Generally negative correlations were observed between the color coordinates and Δ E 00 values for the gold‐colored metal substrate, whereas positive correlations were mainly observed for the silver‐colored metal substrate. Conclusions Masking ability significantly increased with greater material thickness, a trend closely associated with reduced translucency. It was also influenced by both the resin shade and the metal substrate. The P3 shade provided the best masking ability for the tested gold‐colored brass substrate. Under the present in vitro conditions, the tested silver‐colored pure titanium substrate generally produced lower color differences than the tested gold‐colored brass substrate. Clinical Significance Under the present in vitro conditions, a resin thickness of 2 mm may be considered a practical option for masking the tested silver‐colored pure titanium substrate. For the tested gold‐colored brass substrate, masking at 2 mm was shade‐dependent; therefore, careful shade selection or increased resin thickness may be required.

title: One-Dimensional Carbon Nanostructures with Periodic Graphitic Nitrogen Substitution
abstract: Abstract Heteroatom substitution is a powerful route to tune the chemical and electronic properties of carbon nanomaterials. In particular, replacement of an sp2-hybridized carbon atom in the graphene lattice with a nitrogen atom (denoted as graphitic nitrogen) induces substantial changes in the electronic properties. These include changes in the band structure that can influence electronic transport and magnetism. A key requirement for applications is both the periodic and precise incorporation of the heteroatoms in extended carbon lattices. Here, we report the on-surface synthesis and characterization of two one-dimensional carbon nanostructures─a polymer and a graphene nanoribbon─consisting of periodically incorporated graphitic nitrogen atoms. The on-surface reactions toward the formation of the nanostructures were monitored by scanning tunneling microscopy. The bond-resolved chemical structures of the reaction intermediates and products were investigated by atomic force microscopy, which enabled atomic-scale visualization of the graphitic nitrogen sites. The electronic properties of the nanostructures were studied by scanning tunneling spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations. Our analyses revealed the presence of localized nitrogen-centered electronic states in the nanostructures. In the gas phase where the nanostructures are in the neutral charge state, these states undergo spin polarization leading to an open-shell ground state. Upon adsorption on Au(111), the nanostructures exhibit electron transfer to the surface, which resulted in a closed-shell ground state. Our results demonstrate a straightforward and generally applicable route to synthesize graphitic nitrogen-substituted carbon nanomaterials with potential applications in spintronics, catalysis, and energy storage.

title: Bioactive metabolites and botanical preparations from plants used as medicines and foods in ulcerative colitis: a mechanism-oriented narrative review of multi-target regulation
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic relapsing inflammatory bowel disease with a complex pathophysiology involving immune dysregulation, gut microbiota dysbiosis, intestinal barrier impairment, oxidative stress, and regulated cell death. Current therapeutic strategies, including 5-aminosalicylic acid, corticosteroids, immunosuppressants, biologics, and small-molecule agents, have improved disease management; however, incomplete or lost response, adverse effects, and the need for long-term treatment remain important clinical challenges. Bioactive metabolites and botanical preparations from medicinal and food plants have gained increasing attention because of their diverse pharmacological activities and potential to modulate multiple pathological processes involved in UC. This mechanism-oriented narrative review critically summarizes recent evidence on the effects of these plant-derived metabolites, botanical preparations, and combination strategies in UC using a framework that links major UC pathological modules to molecular targets/pathways and functional outcomes, with particular emphasis on anti-inflammatory and antioxidant actions, regulation of ferroptosis and pyroptosis, modulation of autophagy and endoplasmic reticulum stress, protection of the intestinal barrier, and regulation of gut microbiota. The reported mechanisms recurrently converge on signaling networks involving NF-κB, MAPK, Nrf2/ARE, and PI3K/Akt. Evidence from isolated-metabolite cellular studies, extract- and preparation-level studies, animal models, and available human studies varies by the study type. We interpret it according to its mechanistic and translational relevance. Although the available literature indicates that these metabolites may regulate interconnected UC-related pathways through multi-target actions, most mechanistic evidence remains preclinical. Important limitations include incomplete reporting of dose ranges, controls, sample sizes, and quantitative effect estimates; inconsistent documentation of taxonomic authentication and extract characterization; limited metabolite-specific pharmacokinetic and bioavailability data; insufficient translational validation of advanced delivery strategies; variability in microbiota-related findings among experimental models; and limited clinical validation. Further well-designed pharmacological and clinical studies are required to clarify the most robust mechanisms and identify plant-derived metabolites with the greatest potential for further development in UC.

title: A skin-like, all-in-one hydrogel engineered via a supramolecular entangled network reinforced with hydrogen-bond–associated nanodomains
abstract: Hydrogels hold substantial promise for artificial skin in bionic robotics and biomedical devices. However, few hydrogels have a combination of properties comparable to natural human skin. Here, we report a skin-like, all-in-one hydrogel based on a supramolecular entangled network reinforced with hydrogen-bond-associated nanodomains. Within this architecture, hydrogen-bond-associated self-assembled nanodomains, polymer-chain entanglement, dynamic electrostatic interactions, and reversible metal-ligand coordination operate cooperatively to endow the network with mechanical robustness and dynamic adaptability. Consequently, the hydrogel reconciles the intrinsic trade-offs among mechanical properties, multiple functions, and multimodal perception. Its integrated performance compares favorably with that of other advanced hydrogels and even biological skin. To demonstrate its potential applications, we constructed an artificial skin using our hydrogel, which facilitates interaction with the surrounding environment, including monitoring respiration, detecting motion, and manipulating robotic grippers. These results pave the way for versatile hydrogels that replicate the unparalleled combinatory properties of natural skin more precisely for diverse intelligent applications.

title: Linear Supramolecular Polymer of Benzene‐1,3,5‐Tricarboxamides Bearing Two‐Armed Amphiphilic Side Chains in the Bulk State and in Aqueous Solution
abstract: ABSTRACT Here, we report the characterization of C 3 ‐symmetric benzene‐1,3,5‐tricarboxamide (BTA) derivatives bearing symmetrically two‐armed amphiphilic chains adjacent to the amide, which were designed to inhibit side chain crystallization of supramolecular polymers in the bulk state at ambient temperature. IR spectroscopy confirmed the formation of triple hydrogen‐bonded supramolecular polymer chains, and XRD suggested two‐dimensional hexagonal packing. DSC showed side‐chain melting below room temperature, indicating suppressed crystallization. By contrast, the linear side‐chain analogs displayed multiple amide bands in their IR spectra and multiple reflections in XRD. N , N′ , N″ ‐tris(3,6,20,23‐tetraoxa‐1,25‐dihydroxy‐13‐pentacosyl)‐BTA having two‐armed side chains terminated with hydroxyl groups (THBTA) displayed amorphous structure from −80°C to 220°C, exhibiting a hypsochromic shift in UV–vis and marked 1 H‐NMR signal broadening upon dissolution in (heavy) water, consistent with H‐aggregate supramolecular polymer formation. These results suggest that a branched hydrophobic moiety adjacent to the amide group promotes one‐dimensional supramolecular stacking more effectively than its linear analog during the higher‐order structure formation of BTA derivatives.

title: Graphene-Based Functional Composites: Preparation, Self-Healing Systems and Applications
abstract: Graphene is a two-dimensional carbon nanomaterial with atomically thin layered structure. It shows notable mechanical stiffness, charge mobility, thermal conductivity and molecular barrier performance, making it a valuable reinforcing and functionalizing phase for advanced composite systems. Over the past decade, researchers have developed various graphene-incorporated functional composites for applications including self-healing polymers, electrochemical sensors, energy storage electrodes, separation membranes and structural laminates. This review examines mainstream synthesis routes and surface modification approaches for graphene and graphene oxide (GO), focusing on three self-healing composite platforms: polyurethane matrices, hydrogel networks and cementitious materials. For each system, fabrication methods, structure-property relationships and repair mechanisms are discussed. The review also covers applications of graphene-based materials in food safety sensing, lithium-ion battery anodes, water treatment membranes and aerospace structural composites. Despite progress, bottlenecks remain, including poor nanofiller dispersion, weak interfacial adhesion, batch-to-batch variability and high manufacturing cost. These issues limit translation from laboratory demonstrations to industrial use. Optimization strategies are proposed, including hierarchical structural design, precision interface engineering and scalable green manufacturing. This work provides a reference for performance optimization and practical application of graphene-based functional composites.

title: Ionic Liquids‐Mediated Decarboxylation Reactions
abstract: ABSTRACT Decarboxylation is a key process in organic chemistry, wherein a carboxyl group is removed in the form of carbon dioxide. Due to cutting‐edge research in the field of decarboxylation, the green chemistry matrices involving methods have always attracted chemists. Recently, ionic liquids (ILs) demonstrated a very efficient role for the decarboxylation reactions with their unbeatable properties, like negligible vapor pressure and their tunable nature, which can be adjusted to help in dissolving substrates. The adjustable properties of ILs further express them as designer solvents, and additionally, their hydrogen‐bonding capabilities speed up the organic reactions, leading to enhanced performances. Their nonvolatile nature further makes them eco‐friendly and easy to handle, as the product gets separated effortlessly, and hence can be recycled and reused. Current review focuses on the investigation studies articulating ILs in decarboxylation reactions, with scaffolds bearing carboxyl groups such as carboxylic acids, β ‐keto acids, malonic acids, and aromatic carboxylic acids. Basically, ILs are a big step forward in decarboxylation chemistry offering a flexible and eco‐friendly platform. The ongoing research is bound to uncover even more exciting possibilities for sustainable synthesis, making ILs an eco‐friendly tool in modern organic chemistry.

title: Uncovering the thermolysis conversion mechanisms of 3D nanoprinted silica glass
abstract: Abstract Thermal conversion post-processing routes expand two-photon polymerization (2PP) 3D printing from polymers to inorganics, enabling free-form micro- and nanostructures from a growing bandwidth of glasses, ceramics and metals. Yet, limited knowledge on precise transformation mechanisms remains a key obstacle to advancing the approach towards widespread applicability. This paper establishes a fundamental understanding of the thermal conversion manufacturing of silica glass from hybrid organic-inorganic preforms, 2PP-printed from a polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (POSS) feedstock resist. We present correlated thermal, mechanical, and spectroscopic analyses, which resolve key microstructural transformations and resulting dimensional, chromatic and mechanical mechanisms. The thermolysis accesses a wide range of mechanical properties from compliant rubber-like to ceramic-hard with an ultra-high tensile strength of 6 GPa. The introduced correlative methodology and obtained understanding are expected to translate across different routes, providing fundamental groundwork for the rational design of advanced thermal conversion protocols for the precision manufacturing of 3D high-fidelity structures.

title: Insights on the adsorption of malachite green behavior using a bio-inorganic composite of chitosan-cellulose itaconate/nickel oxide
abstract: Abstract The detrimental impacts of dye-containing wastewater discharge on aquatic ecosystems and water quality make it a major environmental concern. The newly synthesized matrix that composed of chitosan-crosslinked cellulose itaconate (CS–CLI) integrated with nickel oxide (NiO) nanoparticles was tested in the removal of malachite green (MG) dye from aqueous solutions. Both surface and core structure of all adsorbents were examined, moreover, different factors affecting the adsorption process such as pH, temperature, contact time, and initial dye concentration were assessed using batch adsorption mode. The findings showed that operating parameters had a significant impact on adsorption efficacy, with optimal removal occurring at pH 7 and 25 °C. At 5 mg/L MG, the removal percentages reached 91% for CS–CLI, 88.9% for NiO, and 81.8% for CS–CLI/NiO, under conditions of pH 7 and 25 °C. The composite's highest adsorption capacity was 11.56 mg/g. Chemisorption was a significant factor in dye uptake, according to kinetic tests that demonstrated the adsorption process followed the pseudo-second-order model. A multi-step adsorption mechanism comprising both surface adsorption and diffusion within the adsorbent structure was proposed by intraparticle diffusion studies. The Freundlich isotherm model provided a more accurate description of equilibrium data, suggesting multilayer adsorption on a heterogeneous surface. The Langmuir isotherm provided the best explanation for the equilibrium results, and adsorption kinetics strongly correlated with the pseudo-second-order model (R 2 = 0.999). It was discovered that the greatest adsorption capacities were 18 mg/g for CS–CLI/NiO, 23.4 mg/g for CS–CLI, and 36.1 mg/g for NiO. Overall, the results show that the CS–CLI/NiO composite is a viable, reasonably priced, and environmentally benign adsorbent for the treatment of dye-contaminated wastewater.

title: Janus Oil–Water Separation Membranes: Synthesis Approaches, Multifunctional Progress and Prospective Challenges
abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid industrialization produces massive oily wastewater and frequent marine oil spills, severely damaging ecosystems and human health. Conventional oil–water separation membranes are restricted by single functions, low efficiency, and severe fouling, failing to cope with complex working environments. Featuring asymmetric wettability and multi‐functionality, Janus separation membranes create a new route for high‐efficiency, energy‐saving, and sustainable oil–water treatment. This review systematically summarizes advances in this underreviewed field. It first introduces the origin and development of the Janus concept, then discusses two dominant fabrication methods: layer‐by‐layer self‐assembly and asymmetric chemical functionalization, covering electrospinning, chemical etching, and surface modification, alongside each method's merits and drawbacks. Beyond basic separation, we overview integrated multifunctions including desalination, heavy metal capture, stimuli responsiveness, antibacterial, and self‐cleaning capacities. Critical bottlenecks concerning material stability, fabrication cost and scalable manufacturing are analyzed, followed by prospects of novel substrates, intelligent responsive membranes and eco‐friendly fabrication. This review delivers systematic theoretical guidance and technical references to boost structural optimization, separation performance, and real‐world engineering deployment of Janus oil–water separation membranes.

title: Ultra-swelling pH-responsive hybrid hydrogel for oral heparin delivery
abstract: Oral delivery of heparin remains challenging because of poor stability and limited site-specific release within the gastrointestinal tract. Herein, an ultra-swelling pH-responsive hybrid hydrogel based on chitosan, acrylic acid, and 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA) was developed through low-temperature redox-initiated graft copolymerization and statistically optimized using a Box–Behnken design. The effects of the monomer-to-chitosan ratio, initiator concentration, and crosslinker content on hydrogel performance were systematically evaluated. Structural, morphological, and thermal characteristics were confirmed by FTIR, XRD, SEM, DSC, and TGA analyses. The optimized hydrogel exhibited a highly porous architecture and an exceptional swelling ratio exceeding 4000% under near-neutral conditions while maintaining limited swelling in acidic media. Heparin loading and in vitro release studies demonstrated minimal drug release at gastric pH and rapid, sustained release at neutral to mildly alkaline pH, reflecting the transition from stomach to intestinal environments. The combination of statistical optimization, pronounced pH responsiveness, and selective heparin release highlights the advantages of this hydrogel over conventional formulations. These findings establish the optimized chitosan-g-poly(AA-co-HEMA) hydrogel as a promising platform for oral delivery of heparin and other pH-sensitive therapeutics requiring controlled gastrointestinal release.

title: Transient structural evolution during electrochemical doping revealed by time‐aligned operando GIWAXS on organic mixed ionic electronic conductors
abstract: Abstract Organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs) exhibit dynamic structural transformations during electrochemical doping, critically impacting device performance in applications such as bioelectronics and neuromorphic computing. While operando grazing‐incidence wide‐angle X‐ray scattering (GIWAXS) has emerged as a powerful tool to probe such changes, its temporal resolution remains fundamentally mismatched with the rapid ion dynamics in OMIECs, often obscuring transient microstructural states. Here, we introduce a time‐aligned operando GIWAXS methodology that bridges this gap by extending the electrochemical doping time constant through engineered device geometry. This enables real‐time tracking of structural evolution during abrupt doping conditions. Using poly(2‐(3,3′‐bis(2‐(2‐(2‐methoxyethoxy)ethoxy)ethoxy)‐[2,2′‐bithiophen]‐5‐yl)thieno[3,2‐b]thiophene) polymers with distinct molecular weights, we reveal that the microstructural response under abrupt biasing diverges significantly from that observed under conventional voltage‐sweeping conditions. Notably, abrupt doping induces intercalation pathways and reorientation behaviors not captured in quasi‐equilibrium measurements. Our approach provides direct insight into doping‐pathway‐dependent structural dynamics and offers a generalizable strategy for resolving rapid ion–polymer interactions in functional OMIEC systems. These findings highlight the importance of kinetic control in operando measurements and inform the rational design of mixed‐conducting polymer devices for transient or pulse‐driven applications. image

title: An Approach to Predict Thermal Degradation Characteristics of Ethylene Propylene Diene Monomer and Rocasin Elastomers Under Extreme Heating Rate for High‐Temperature Insulation Application
abstract: ABSTRACT The thermal degradation behavior of EPDM and Rocasin elastomers at heating rates far exceeding the capability of conventional thermogravimetric analysis (TGA; limited to approximately 200°C/min) remains poorly characterized, despite the critical role of these materials in rocket motor insulation, cable sheathing, and high‐temperature sealing applications. This study addresses that gap by deriving thermal degradation kinetics from TGA experiments at β = 10–150°C/min under a nitrogen atmosphere and extending the validated models to simulate degradation behavior at extreme heating rates of 500–2000°C/min, mainly for rocket motor applications. In this study, EPDM and Rocasin elastomers are heated to 1000°C at different heating rates from 10 to 150°C/min. The degradation mechanisms across various temperature ranges were studied along with the kinetic models to elucidate the kinetic parameters. The degradation pattern of the materials was simulated and compared with the data within the limits of TGA. Furthermore, these parameters were used to construct a preliminary kinetic‐extrapolation framework for predicting degradation behavior beyond the limits of conventional TGA, which may serve as input for subsequent coupled transient heat transfer and ablation modeling of insulation systems.

title: Precise modular engineering of neutral organometallic rectangles from binuclear palladacycles via hierarchical assembly strategy
abstract: Abstract Metallosupramolecular assembly provides a powerful strategy for the precise construction of well-defined architectures with diverse topologies and functionalities. However, the construction of neutral organometallic architectures supported by robust metal-carbon bonds remains underdeveloped, largely because kinetic persistence limits the reversible structural correction required for conventional self-assembly. Herein, we employ binuclear palladacycles as intrinsically neutral and geometrically preorganized building blocks and develop a hierarchical assembly strategy that temporally separates geometric programming, scaffold editing, and topology locking. Through a polymerization-cleavage-assembly process, cyclopalladated polymers are converted into discrete binuclear precursors while retaining their programmed geometrical information. Subsequent trans-effect-directed N -heterocyclic carbene ligation affords a series of size-tunable, kinetically robust, and neutral organometallic rectangles. The resulting architectures are fully characterized by spectroscopic methods and single crystal X-ray diffraction analyses. Moreover, single crystal X-ray diffraction identifies guest-mediated breathing-like geometric deformations in the solid state, driven by exo-wall π-π stacking and charge-transfer interactions with both electron-rich and electron-deficient planar guests. This work establishes a hierarchical construction principle for accessing discrete neutral organometallic architectures by separating geometric programming from the final locking of the topology through strong bond formation, while demonstrating that local geometric adaptation can occur without disrupting the framework connectivity established by Pd-C bonds.

title: Marine Algae‐Derived Starch and Polysaccharides for Sustainable Bioplastics: Processing, Properties, Environmental Performance, and Future Prospects
abstract: ABSTRACT Marine algae present a promising foundation for developing sustainable bioplastics, distinguished by rapid growth, abundant carbohydrates, and minimal land and freshwater demands. This paper examines the utilization of marine algae‐derived starch and other polysaccharides in bioplastic manufacturing, encompassing algal characteristics, carbohydrate and polysaccharide recovery, bioplastic formulation and properties, and environmental implications. Marine algae‐derived starch and polysaccharides have emerged as promising raw materials for bioplastic development because of their carbohydrate content, functional diversity, and potential for integration into marine biorefinery systems. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of the potential of algae‐based starch in bioplastic production, exploring algal biology, starch extraction processes, and the fabrication and performance of algal bioplastics. Recent advancements, practical applications, and the challenges associated with scaling up marine algae‐based bioplastics are evaluated. Despite significant progress, several challenges continue to hinder large‐scale commercialization, including feedstock variability, energy‐intensive drying and extraction processes, limited moisture resistance, and the absence of standardized end‐of‐life management frameworks. This review critically evaluates these barriers and identifies future research directions aimed at improving material performance, process sustainability, and industrial scalability. The review underscores the potential of marine algae as a sustainable resource for mitigating plastic pollution and advancing green technologies.

title: Feedstock-Dependent Properties of Degradable Thermosets Derived from Kraft Lignins and Epoxidized Linseed Oil
abstract: Abstract Brittleness and poor network control limit lignin-based thermosets. Highly bio-based thermosets (∼90% bio-based content) were prepared from oxidized spruce and eucalyptus kraft lignins and epoxidized linseed oil (ELO) via acid−epoxide curing, and poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) was incorporated to improve toughness, yielding homogeneous networks with high gel content (>88%). Both thermosets showed comparable thermal stability (tan δ peak 93−109 °C; degradation onset above 250 °C), while lignin origin caused subtle differences in crosslinking efficiency, wettability, and thermomechanical behavior. WAXS revealed sandwich (89−91%) and T-shaped π−π stacking in both systems. Under alkaline conditions, rapid ester hydrolysis dissolved the network within 48 h, whereas minor mass loss occurred under near-neutral conditions. Spectroscopy indicated cleavage of the ester crosslinks, with the aromatic lignin framework largely intact, and decreased T-shaped stacking in spruce-derived thermosets. These results show how lignin origin and network design can tune material properties and end-of-life behavior.

title: Graphene‑based nanomaterials for drug delivery: Design strategies, mechanisms and clinical perspectives (Review)
abstract: Graphene-based nanomaterials have emerged as a versatile platform for tumour-targeted drug delivery owing to their unique physicochemical properties, including large specific surface area, structural flexibility and tuneable surface chemistry.Graphene oxide (GO) and reduced GO have been extensively investigated as drug carriers owing to their high loading capacity and multifunctionality.Recent advances in nanoscale engineering and surface functionalisation have enabled precise control over drug loading, targeting and release behaviour, thereby improving therapeutic efficacy while minimising systemic toxicity.The present review provides a comprehensive and mechanism-oriented overview of graphene-based nanocarriers, focusing on their structural features, synthesis methods, functionalisation strategies, drug loading and tumour-targeting approaches, and stimuli-responsive release behaviours.Compared with conventional descriptions of graphene-based carriers, the present review highlights the emerging transition from passive delivery systems towards rationally engineered and stimuli-programmed nanomedicine platforms.Furthermore, key challenges related to colloidal stability, toxicity, biodegradability, in vivo fate and clinical translation are critically discussed.By linking advanced design strategies with mechanistic understanding and translational insights, the present review aims to guide the development of safer, more reliable and clinically relevant graphene-based nanomedicines for precision cancer therapy.Contents 1. Introduction 2. Synthesis of graphene and its derivatives 3. Graphene and its derivatives in drug delivery 4. Conclusion and prospects

title: Programmable hydrogel-nanocapsule protein delivery system targeting dense cartilage regeneration for osteoarthritis therapy
abstract: The clinical translation of protein therapeutics for osteoarthritis has been hampered by rapid synovial clearance, poor penetration into cartilage, and insufficient retention under joint loading. In this work, we develop hydro/nano-bFGF, a programmable system that integrates an FGF-loaded nanocapsule (nano-bFGF) with an injectable, cartilage-adhesive hydrogel. Nano-bFGF is generated through interfacial polymerization of monomers with enzyme-cleavable crosslinkers directly on the protein surface, forming a nanoscale shell that preserves bioactivity while enabling pathology-specific disassembly. The hydrogel anchors nano-bFGF to the cartilage surface and undergoes gradual degradation in response to disease-associated enzymatic activity, allowing spatiotemporally programmed release aligned with the joint microenvironment. This spatiotemporally controlled design enhances intra-cartilage transport, prolongs local retention, and maintains growth factor functionality. In human osteoarthritic cartilage explants, nano-bFGF doubles glycosaminoglycan deposition and triples type II collagen expression. In a rat model, hydro/nano-bFGF restores cartilage integrity, preserves subchondral bone architecture, and achieves restoration of cartilage thickness. Owing to its modular design, this strategy is broadly adaptable to diverse protein therapeutics and degenerative joint diseases, offering a generalizable platform for spatiotemporally precise biologic delivery. In osteoarthritis, protein therapeutics show poor joint retention and cartilage penetration. Here, authors develop a programmable two-stage, enzyme-responsive hydrogel-nanocapsule system to deliver a model protein drug and promote cartilage regeneration.

title: Flavonoids From Sophora tonkinensis Disrupt STING ‐ TBK 1‐ IRF 3 Complex Assembly and Ameliorate Inflammatory Diseases by Modulating c GAS ‐ STING Signaling
abstract: cGAS-STING pathway is a core regulator of innate immunity and inflammatory responses. Aberrant activation of the cGAS-STING pathway is closely associated with the progression of multiple inflammatory disorders. Flavonoids from Sophora tonkinensis (STF) are the main ingredients of this traditional Chinese medicine with definite anti-inflammatory activity, whereas its molecular mechanism against inflammation remains unclear. This work aimed to explore the regulatory effect and underlying molecular mechanism of STF on the cGAS-STING pathway, and verify its therapeutic efficacy on typical inflammatory diseases in vivo. BMDMs and human THP-1 were used for in vitro experiments. Western blot, RT-qPCR, ELISA, Co-IP, and Native-PAGE were performed to detect protein phosphorylation, gene expression, protein-protein interaction, and STING oligomerization. Lipopolysaccharide/D-galactosamine (LPS/D-GalN)-induced acute liver injury and LPS-induced sepsis mouse models were established to evaluate the in vivo anti-inflammatory and organ-protective effects of STF. Serum biochemical detection and gene expression analysis were carried out for in vivo sample evaluation. STF suppressed ISD-triggered activation of the cGAS-STING pathway, as evidenced by reduced phosphorylation of interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3) and STING, as well as decreased expression of downstream inflammatory mediators. Mechanistically, STF did not interfere with STING oligomerization but blocked the assembly of the STING-TBK1 complex and the interaction between IRF3 and TBK1. In vivo experiments demonstrated that STF dose-dependently alleviated hepatic pathological damage and hepatocyte apoptosis in a mouse model of acute liver injury. Furthermore, STF improved survival rates and attenuated multi-organ injury in septic mice by reducing the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines. STF exerts targeted anti-inflammatory activity via disrupting STING-TBK1 and TBK1-IRF3 complex assembly and inhibiting the cGAS-STING signaling cascade. It provides experimental evidence for the clinical application and translational research of Sophora tonkinensis and its flavonoid components in the treatment of cGAS-STING-related inflammatory diseases.

title: Dual Molecularly Imprinted Mesoporous Organosilica Nanoprobes for AI-Assisted Glutathione Redox Ratio Sensing
abstract: Abstract Molecular recognition nanomaterials that directly decode mixture composition remain underdeveloped because chemically related analytes often produce nonlinear and partially overlapping optical responses. Here, dual molecularly imprinted mesoporous organosilica nanoprobes are developed for AI-assisted determination of the glutathione redox ratio. Zwitterion-embedded mesoporous organosilica nanocavities are independently imprinted with reduced glutathione (GSH) or glutathione disulfide (GSSG), followed by pore confinement of blue-emissive graphene quantum dots as fluorescence transducers. The resulting MIMO_GSH-Q and MIMO_GSSG-Q probes generate complementary raw fluorescence fingerprints from mixed GSH/GSSG samples. A deep neural network trained on paired microplate fluorescence intensities performs inverse prediction of τ = [GSH]/[GSSG]. A single test mixture at τ = 0.60, absent from the training ratios, yields a mean predicted ratio of 0.575. These results provide a proof-of-concept demonstration of two-channel ratio inference under the tested conditions, while broader external validation is required to establish its range of applicability. This work demonstrates a trainable nanoporous recognition platform that transforms selective nanoconfined fluorescence responses into quantitative redox-ratio information, providing a general route toward AI-decodable sensing nanomaterials.

title: Canopy light limitation under close planting is associated with reduced wheat basal stem strength, phenylpropanoid attenuation, and lignin monomer remodeling
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lodging is a major factor limiting wheat yield improvement under high-density cultivation and is closely associated with canopy low light conditions caused by close planting. Canopy light limitation under close planting can suppress stem lignification and weaken mechanical strength, yet the structural and metabolic basis of this response remains insufficiently resolved. A two-season field-embedded pot experiment compared sparse planting (SP), close planting (CP), and close planting with supplemental lighting (CP + L), integrating physiological, mechanical, biochemical, transcriptomic, and metabolomic analyses. RESULTS: Compared with SP, CP reduced the net photosynthetic rate of the third to fifth leaves by 24.59-26.43%, decreased stem diameter and breaking moment, and increased the lodging index. Total lignin content declined by 36.34%, and the G-type lignin-derived aldehyde showed the greatest reduction, resulting in a 33.82% increase in the S/G ratio. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses indicated coordinated attenuation of photosynthetic carbon fixation, secondary cell wall formation, and phenylpropanoid-related processes under CP. These changes were accompanied by lower activities of PAL, 4CL, C4H, and CCR and reduced accumulation of hydroxycinnamic acid derivatives and monolignol-related intermediates. Gene-metabolite and TF-structural gene analyses identified treatment-dependent co-variation patterns within the phenylpropanoid pathway. Supplemental lighting increased leaf photosynthetic rates by 20.56-27.39% and partially restored lignin-related enzyme activities, molecular responses, total lignin content, and stem mechanical performance without changing planting density. CONCLUSIONS: Close planting was associated with reduced basal stem strength, lower lignification, and attenuation of phenylpropanoid-lignin metabolism. The partial recovery under CP + L supports an important contribution of within-canopy light availability to these responses. These findings highlight canopy light management as a potential strategy for improving wheat lodging resistance under high-density cultivation.

title: Preparation of solvent-based fluorine–silicon modified acrylate and its application in specialty paper
abstract: Conventional starch and polyvinyl alcohol sizing agents rely on hydrogen bonding, but are susceptible to temperature and humidity, limiting their use in specialty papers such as banknotes. To address this, we synthesized a fluorine–silicon modified acrylate via radical copolymerization of hexafluorobutyl methacrylate (HFBMA) and silane coupling agents (KH570 and KH560) with common acrylate monomers, using ethanol as solvent. HFBMA lowers surface energy through C–F bond surface segregation, while the silane components form Si–O–Si networks and silanol groups that strengthen hydrogen bonding with cellulose fibers. Upon drying, the fluorinated and siloxane segments migrate to the paper surface and assemble into a hydrophobic barrier. Among three systems (F3, Si 570 -F3, and Si 560 -F3), the optimized Si 560 -F3 at 5% dosage increased tensile strength from 28.1 to 47.8 MPa (+70.1%), reduced water absorption from 29.1% to 5.5% (−81.1%), and raised water contact angle from 85° to 122°. These results confirm that this sizing agent effectively enhances both mechanical strength and water resistance for specialty paper.

title: Collagen-based medical devices: technological basis and clinical studies
abstract: Despite the widespread use of collagen-based medical devices in clinical practice, their clinical efficacy is often analyzed independently from the technological aspects that largely determine the functional capabilities and limitations of a specific product. In this review, the authors formulated technical requirements for collagen-based medical devices across seven clinical areas: dentistry, dermatology, ophthalmology, gastroenterology, neurosurgery, general surgery, traumatology and orthopedics. For each area, clinical studies registered in ClinicalTrials.gov and reported in the relevant scientific literature were analyzed. Product manufacturing technologies and characteristics were identified based on patent searches in the Espacenet and PatentScope databases, as well as data provided by manufacturers. It was demonstrated that collagen-based medical devices should not be regarded as a universal class with an unambiguous regenerative effect. For several clinical indications and specific products, the authors identified neutral or negative clinical outcomes, which were examined from a technological perspective. This approach makes this review valuable for researchers focused on developing new collagen-based products by providing an opportunity to gain both clinical and technical insights and identify relevant research gaps.

title: Structural conservation and expanded functionality of hyper‐stable human serum albumin variants
abstract: Human serum albumin (hSA) is the most abundant protein in human plasma, and its pharmacological properties, such as long plasma half-life mediated by the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) and its ability to bind endogenous and exogenous molecules, make it attractive for biotechnological applications. Currently, most wild type (WT) SAs are derived from human or bovine serum or produced in yeast and mammalian cells. Although well established, these methods are costly, difficult to reproduce, and not environmentally sustainable. Building on a previous study to design highly mutated hSA sequences, we extend the validation through an in-depth analysis of three engineered hSA variants: hSA1, hSA2, and hSA3, containing 16, 25, or 73 amino acid substitutions, respectively. These variants were designed for enhanced solubility, stability, and expression in Escherichia coli. All three variants showed low micromolar affinities for hFcRn at pH 5.5, and negligible binding at pH 7.4. In a human endothelial cell-based recycling assay (HERA), the engineered hSA variants were recycled by hFcRn to the same extent as hSA isolated from serum. Exploring the properties of canonical drug-binding sites, warfarin affinity was comparable to WT hSA, whereas ibuprofen binding differed. Complementary cytotoxicity assays on human macrophages confirmed negligible toxicity and biocompatibility. The cryo-electron microscopy structure of hSA3 revealed that, despite extensive engineering, the native heart-shape of hSA, folding of domains, and its open conformation were preserved. These findings validate the structural integrity and functional adaptability of engineered hSA variants, underscoring their potential as versatile, animal-free solutions for next-generation therapeutics and biotechnological applications.

title: Effects of Methyl-Substituted Aniline Derivatives on Phase-Separated Bisphenol A-Based-Polybenzoxazine/Polyurethane Two-Way Shape Memory Polymers Behaviors
abstract: Abstract Two-way shape memory polymers (2WSMPs) based on gradient bilayer interpenetrating polymer network (IPN) architectures have attracted increasing attention owing to their ability to undergo reversible actuation without external reprogramming, making them promising candidates for applications such as self-folding structures, soft robotics, and safety circuit breakers. However, the molecular and morphological factors governing gradient architecture formation and their influence on reversible actuation behavior remain insufficiently explored. In this work, gradient bilayer IPNs were constructed in bisphenol A-based polybenzoxazine/polyurethane thermosetting systems by tailoring the benzoxazine phase using aromatic amines with different substitution patterns. A clear correlation between curing kinetics, cross-link density, phase morphology, and reversible actuation behavior was established. Meta-substituted systems (BA-3,5x and BA-mt) exhibited lower ring-opening polymerization temperatures, promoting early stage network formation and phase fixation during curing. The resulting higher cross-link density facilitated the formation of homogeneous benzoxazine-rich domains and distinct gradient bilayer architectures, as confirmed by FTIR, surface hardness, and AFM analyses. In contrast, ortho- and para-substituted systems (BA-ot and BA-pt) showed higher curing temperatures, lower network rigidity, and greater phase heterogeneity, resulting in poorly developed gradient architectures and insufficient structural integrity for reliable actuation. The optimized systems (BA-3,5x/PU and BA-mt/PU) demonstrated excellent reversible deformation, with high shape fixity (∼98%) and shape recovery (∼97–98%). Notably, BA-3,5x/PU exhibited faster recovery behavior (32–38 s) than BA-mt/PU (40–43 s), attributed to its higher cross-link density and more effective gradient bilayer architecture. This study provides correlation insights into gradient bilayer IPN formation and establishes a molecular design strategy for advanced two-way shape memory polymers.

title: Benzoxazine Resins Containing Trifluoroacetylamine: Preparation, Curing Kinetics, and Thermal Properties
abstract: ABSTRACT In order to reduce the polymerization temperature of conventional benzoxazines, three single‐functional benzoxazines (TF‐EBA, TF‐FBA, and TF‐PBA) containing trifluoroacetylamino groups were synthesized. The molecular structures of TF‐EBA, TF‐FBA and TF‐PBAwereconfirmed by Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FT‐IR) and protonNuclearMagnetic Resonance ( 1 H NMR). The curing kinetics of the TF‐BA resins were analyzed by Kissinger and Ozawa methods. The activation energies for the polymerization of TF‐EBA were 80.80 and 84.70 kJ/mol, respectively, which were determined by the Kissinger and the Ozawa methods. The curing behavior was analyzed by Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) and FTIR. After 170°C/1 h + 200°C/3 h heat treatment, the TF‐BA resins were cured completely. Meanwhile, the thermal stability of TF‐BA benzoxazine polymers was evaluated by Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA) and Dynamic Mechanical Analysis (DMA). The glass transition temperatures ( T g ) of the three TF‐BA resins all exceed 200°C. Among them, the T g of TF‐EBA is 276°C, and the T g of TF‐FBA is 282°C. Under N 2 atmosphere, the char yield ( Y c ) of all TF‐BA resins at 800°C is more than 40%. In summary, this study conducted a detailed discussion on the curing kinetics and thermal stability of monofunctional benzoxazines containing trifluoroacetyl amino groups, and it has certain reference value for related work.

title: Comparative Analysis of Poly(Ethylene Glycol) (PEG) and Poly(2‐Ethyl‐2‐Oxazoline) (PEtOx) for Organic Solvent‐Free Lipid Nanoparticle Formulations
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient, biocompatible, and flexible application of CRISPR‐Cas9 remains a major challenge in gene therapy. This study addresses a novel formulation method, focusing on organic solvent‐free lipid nanoparticles for the efficient delivery of CRISPR‐Cas9 components. Therefore, novel stealth lipids comprising the lipid anchor cholesterol hemisuccinate conjugated to poly(2‐ethyl‐2‐oxazoline) (PEtOx) were synthesized and evaluated as a promising in vitro alternative to commercially available poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG)‐based lipids. Our study identified PEtOx‐lipids as markedly more biocompatible compared to PEG‐based analogues (12‐fold reduction in cytotoxicity; 99% reduced hemolytic effect) with high efficiency for mRNA gene delivery. We demonstrate successful CRISPR‐Cas9 activity ex vivo and efficient uptake of PEtOx nanoparticles by macrophages in vivo (66.5% pos. F4/80 + macrophages). Our data demonstrate that PEtOx‐based stealth lipids are a promising alternative to PEG. The resulting LNPs, optimized for fully aqueous manufacturing, address key limitations of current LNP systems, including immunogenicity and the reliance on ethanol‐based production processes.

title: The Boron–Neuron Connection: The Potential of Boron‐Containing Molecules for Treating Incurable Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
abstract: BACKGROUND: ) geometries enable dynamic covalent interactions with biological nucleophiles, making boron-containing compounds (BCCs) attractive pharmacophores that selectively interact with reactive oxygen species (ROS) and are ROS-responsive for therapeutic development. BCCs possess antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and metal-chelating properties that make them attractive candidates for neurodegenerative diseases. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a fatal and multifactorial motor neurodegenerative disorder, is characterized by oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and metal dyshomeostasis, providing a strong rationale for exploring boron-based therapeutics. METHODS: This review examines current literature on B chemistry, pharmacology, and translational applications, with emphasis on mechanisms relevant to ALS pathogenesis. This review focuses on ROS-responsive B scaffolds, blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, neuroprotective mechanisms, hormonal modulation, metal chelation, and emerging preclinical evidence supporting boron-based interventions. CONCLUSIONS: BCCs represent a promising yet underexplored therapeutic platform for ALS and related neurodegenerative disorders. Their ROS-responsive, redox-modulating, and neuroprotective properties, combined with favorable CNS drug-like pharmacokinetics, offer a mechanistically distinct approach to disease modification. Emerging preclinical evidence strongly supports further translational investigation.

title: Dynamic Supramolecular Cryptomaterials for Compositional Encoding and Mechanical Decryption
abstract: ABSTRACT Advanced cryptomaterials capable of storing concealed information and selectively revealing it through dynamic pathways are desirable for next‐generation cryptography. However, simultaneously achieving high‐dimensional information encoding, scalable material fabrication, and secure yet equipment‐free decryption remains an unresolved challenge. Herein, we present a class of dynamic supramolecular cryptomaterials (DSCs) that couple compositional encoding with mechanical decryption, establishing a fundamentally different cryptographic paradigm. Multi‐component functionalized colloids are embedded within polymer matrices via dynamic supramolecular interactions, producing visually indistinguishable precursor materials in which the encoded information is completely concealed. Upon prescribed oscillatory shearing stimulus, transient supramolecular networks are selectively activated, driving a disorder‐to‐order transition and leading to highly ordered superstructures with formulation‐specific optical fingerprints, jointly governed by material composition and the mechanical activation. By independently programming composition, including the colloids and polymer, the DSCs enable continuous structural‐color regulation across 410–753 nm while simultaneously tailoring color saturation and brightness. The multidimensional compositional space provides exceptional information density, with each pixel capable of encoding up to 393 identities. This work establishes a general materials design strategy that transforms composition from a passive formulation parameter into an active information carrier and introduces mechanically programmable supramolecular cryptomaterials as a scalable platform for high‐security information encryption and advanced anti‐counterfeiting.

title: Biodegradable polymer composites: Blend design, compatibilization strategies, reinforcement approaches and future perspective
abstract: The escalating environmental burden of fossil-based plastics and the urgent demand for sustainable materials have intensified research into biodegradable polymer composites as viable alternatives. Sustainable biodegradable polymer composites offer the potential to combine eco-friendly end-of-life behaviour with enhanced mechanical, thermal and functional properties. However, intrinsic limitations such as brittleness, immiscibility in blends and inadequate interfacial adhesion present significant challenges for broader application. To overcome these hurdles, recent studies emphasize strategic polymer blending, compatibilization mechanisms and reinforcement approaches. Biodegradable blends, particularly those based on polylactic acid, polyhydroxyalkanoates, polybutylene succinate/polybutylene adipate-terephthalate and thermoplastic starch, have been engineered to tailor performance via optimized phase morphology and synergistic property combinations. Compatibilizers such as maleated agents, reactive coupling systems and emerging bio-based compatibilizers are instrumental in improving miscibility and interfacial interactions. Reinforcements ranging from natural fibers and agro-waste fillers to nanofillers further enhance composite stiffness, toughness, barrier and functional behaviours. These strategies highlights structure-property relationships and discusses sustainability assessments including biodegradation pathways and circular economy integration. Future research directions focus on green processing, advanced compatibilizer design and multifunctional composite systems to accelerate the transition from laboratory innovation to industrially relevant sustainable solutions.

title: Recent advances in the use of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) as delivery vectors for mRNA
abstract: Abstract Therapeutic mRNA has demonstrated great promise in infectious disease vaccines, cancer immunotherapy, and protein replacement therapies. However, its clinical translation is hampered by intrinsic limitations, including rapid degradation, poor membrane permeability, extremely low endosomal escape, lack of tissue specificity, and potential immunogenicity. Naked mRNA alone is insufficient to overcome these challenges, which has driven the emergence of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) as the leading clinical-grade delivery platform. LNPs employ a four-component system: ionizable lipids for encapsulation and pH-responsive fusion; helper phospholipids and cholesterol for structural integrity and membrane fluidity; and PEGylated lipids for colloidal stability and prolonged circulation. This review systematically addresses LNP composition, structure–activity relationships, and the interplay with extrinsic factors—including administration routes, targeting ligands, immunostimulant co-delivery, and organ tropism (liver, spleen, lungs, lymph nodes)—that collectively govern mRNA biodistribution and therapeutic efficacy. Nonetheless, several major bottlenecks persist, such as unclear endosomal escape mechanisms, PEG-related immune interference, obstacles to extrahepatic delivery, manufacturing complexities, and challenges in AI-driven lipid design. Future progress will rely on integrating rational design, high-throughput screening, and engineering innovations to develop precision delivery systems that are safe, efficient, and amenable to repeated administration—thereby fully unlocking the clinical potential of mRNA-based therapies.

title: Reproducibility and Batch-Dependent Variability in Polymer-Based Nanocarriers
abstract: Abstract Polymers are essential functional constituents in most nanomedicines. While frequently treated conceptually as defined compounds in this respect, polymers are intrinsically heterogeneous materials, as they arise from statistical chain growth. Consequently, batch-to-batch variability is inherent to polymers. While this aspect is often overlooked, it potentially impacts reproducibility in downstream processes, particularly in systems that heavily rely on polymers, such as polymeric micelles. To systematically capture the impact of batch-to-batch variability in such systems, we compare five batches each of three different amphiphilic poly(2-oxazoline)/poly(2-oxazine) (POx/POzi) block copolymers synthesized in three independent laboratories. In aqueous solution, all batches formed micelles. Minor differences in hydrodynamic size and critical micelle concentration, however, could not be readily deduced from standard physicochemical data. Drug solubilization up to a certain level proved to be an intrinsic and reproducible property of a given POx/POzi copolymer. However, individual batches displayed enhanced loading, which was not representative of the reliably achievable solubilization capacity. Cell viability assays indicated mostly consistent profiles across batches, yet rare nonrepresentative batches with altered responses did occur. Overall, our findings demonstrate reproducible baseline behavior alongside an inherent and sometimes pronounced batch-dependent component, which can critically confound interpretation and overstate reliability when only single batches are examined.

title: [Research advances in nanobiotechnology targeting reactive oxygen species for radiation injury repair].
abstract: The burst generation of reactive oxygen species serves as a key driver of radiation injury. Efficient scavenging of excessive reactive oxygen species and restoration of redox homeostasis represent a critical therapeutic strategy for radiation injury repair. However, conventional antioxidants have limitations such as poor stability, weak targeting capability, and low bioavailability. Nanomaterials, distinguished by their unique size effects, high specific surface area, and functional plasticity, have brought new ideas for this field. This review summarizes the pathological mechanisms of reactive oxygen species-mediated radiation injury, then systematically reviews the research progress on strategies targeting reactive oxygen species to modulate radiation injury repair based on nanomaterial types, delves into the molecular mechanisms and application prospects of nanomaterials in scavenging reactive oxygen species, breaking the inflammatory cycle, and promoting tissue regeneration, and finally provides an outlook on the challenges of clinical translation and future directions for intelligent nanomedicines, with the aim of providing theoretical references and research ideas for breaking through the limitations of traditional antioxidants and advancing mechanistic research and clinical translation in the protection and repair of radiation injury.

title: Strain and Chirality: Catalytic Asymmetric Synthesis of Planar Chiral [2.2]Paracyclophanes
abstract: Planar‐chiral [2.2]paracyclophanes occupy a distinctive position in modern chemistry because their rigid cofacial aromatic architecture connects molecular shape, through‐space electronic communication and chirality within a compact scaffold. These features have made them valuable in asymmetric catalysis, ligand and organocatalyst design, optoelectronic materials and chiroptical systems. However, the preparation of enantioenriched [2.2]paracyclophanes has historically relied on resolution‐based approaches, limiting both efficiency and structural diversification. Catalytic asymmetric synthesis has recently opened new opportunities for the direct construction of planar chirality in [2.2]paracyclophane frameworks, particularly through desymmetrization of prochiral substrates. This Review summarizes recent progress in the catalytic asymmetric synthesis of planar‐chiral [2.2]paracyclophanes, discusses the key structural and mechanistic features underlying enantioinduction, and outlines future directions for this rapidly evolving field. Particular attention is given to how substrate topology, catalyst design and reaction pathway govern stereocontrol, and to how the resulting enantioenriched scaffolds can serve as functional building blocks for catalysis, molecular design and chiral materials.

title: Programmable roll-to-roll laser processing for high value application of low-grade carbon fiber materials
abstract: Abstract Growing production of carbon fibers generates substantial short-chopped fibers that are difficult for high-value use due to their structural discontinuity. Carbon fiber felts offer potential, yet weak inter-fiber bonding and poor conductivity limit the performance. We report a roll‑to‑roll laser processing strategy that uses a liquid precursor to form laser‑induced graphene at fiber‑fiber interfaces, creating conductive pathways and mechanical interconnections. This approach increases tensile strength from 4.1 to 32.2 MPa and electrical conductivity from 1224.0 to 15151.5 S/m. The resulting films demonstrate efficient electrothermal de‑icing and, after copper deposition, lightning strike protection with a damage area of 9657 mm² and depth of 0.4 mm, comparable to aluminum mesh but with 15% lower weight. A custom‑built laser platform enables scalable production. Here, we show the conversion of low‑grade carbon fibers into lightweight, functional films for aerospace applications via scalable laser processing.

title: Benzoxazine Functionalization of CO2-Derived Block Copolymers toward High-Performance Thermosets through Cooperative Covalent Crosslinking and Hydrogen Bonding
abstract: Abstract CO2-derived aliphatic polycarbonates have attracted considerable attention as sustainable polymeric materials; however, their relatively low glass transition temperature and limited thermal stability restrict their applications in high-performance engineering materials. Herein, a series of benzoxazine-functionalized CO2-derived block copolymers, poly(cyclohexene carbonate)-b-poly(styrene-alt-1-(3-phenyl-3,4-dihydro-2H-benzoxazin-6-yl)-1H-pyrrole-2,5-dione) (PCHC-b-PSHPMIBZ), were successfully synthesized through sequential ring-opening copolymerization (ROCOP) of cyclohexene oxide and CO2 and reversible addition–fragmentation chain-transfer (RAFT) polymerization. The thermal properties of the resulting block copolymers were systematically tailored by varying the PSHPMIBZ contents followed by thermal ring-opening polymerization (ROP). During thermal curing, the benzoxazine units simultaneously generated a covalently crosslinked network and abundant phenolic hydroxyl groups, which established extensive intermolecular and intramolecular hydrogen-bonding interactions with neighboring carbonate and imide carbonyl groups. The thermal ROP mechanism and structural evolution were comprehensively elucidated using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), in situ Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, two-dimensional (2D) correlation FTIR spectroscopy, and solid-state 13C NMR spectroscopy. These complementary analyses revealed that hydrogen-bonding formation occurred immediately following benzoxazine ring opening, producing a hierarchical dual-network architecture composed of covalent crosslinks and supramolecular hydrogen bonds. Consequently, the glass transition temperature of PCHC-b-PSHPMIBZ51 increased dramatically from 115 to 199 °C, while the char yield increased from 0.9 wt % for the corresponding PCHC-b-PSHPMI51 copolymer to 25.3 wt %, and further to 38.3 wt % after post-curing at 270 °C. The cured block copolymers retained homogeneous morphology despite extensive crosslinking, demonstrating that benzoxazine functionalization provides an effective molecular design strategy for converting sustainable CO2-derived polycarbonate block copolymers into thermosetting materials with substantially elevated glass transition temperatures and enhanced thermal resistance.

title: A Topological Trade-Off: Cyclic Poly(2-methyl-2-oxazoline) Shells Enhance Opsonization and Macrophage Uptake of Nanoparticles Despite Superior Protein Repellent Properties
abstract: Abstract Organically modified silica (ORMOSIL) nanoparticles functionalized with linear poly(2-methyl-2-oxazoline) (L-PMOXA NPs) promote C3b/iC3b-mediated uptake by human myeloid leukocytes in human serum. We tested if NPs functionalized with cyclic PMOXA (C-PMOXA NPs) prevent this effect. The adsorption of human and pig serum proteins to C-PMOXA NPs was reduced compared to L-PMOXA NPs. However, C-PMOXA NPs bound IgG3, IgG1, and complement factors C1q, properdin, and CFAB and activated complement more than L-PMOXA NPs. Consistently, monocytes and macrophages captured C-PMOXA NPs more efficiently than L-PMOXA NPs, while lymphocytes exhibited markedly lower binding of NPs independently of their polymer shells. Despite superior protein repellent properties, cyclic PMOXA shells promote the recruitment of immune agonists and enhance NP opsonization. These limitations may represent a biological bottleneck in designing improved stealth NPs based on the topological modulations of their polymer shells.

title: Dye-altered alumina. Design and control of the optical properties of nanoporous anodic alumina platforms infiltrated with natural and synthetic organic dyes
abstract: Emission control and enhancement of emitters are cornerstones of modern light-emitting, display, and optical sensing technologies. Over the past decades, research on stained nanoporous anodic alumina (NAA) platforms for optical and photonic applications has evolved from understanding the NAA structure-dye property correlations to the design of photoluminescent sensors. In particular, correlating optical properties with geometrical features of the NAA has become a major focus. Because NAA can effectively immobilise molecules smaller than its pores such as organic dyes, these nanoporous solid-state platforms could be used as light-emitting devices, dye-sensitised solar cells, protonation-deprotonation indicators, and photoluminescent sensors. They have also demonstrated potential for enhancing light-matter interactions through slowing light near the photonic bandgap, leading to narrowband laser action. In recent years, many scientific papers have been published on the concept, fabrication, and characterisation of stained NAA platforms with uniform and modulated nanopore diameters. This review highlights the transformative potential of stained NAA platforms, focusing on the critical role played by organic dyes, which act as gain media immobilised in the ordered nanostructures, in generating the desired emissions. It aims to trace the evolution of this field and provide an accessible overview for researchers working on or interested in stained NAA platforms. By synthesising previous advances, we provide a forward-looking perspective on the development of stained NAA platforms, proposing a greater focus on interactions dye-dye and dye-NAA interactions.

title: Exploring the Impact of Processing Techniques on the Structural and Mechanical Properties of Multifunctional Phthalonitrile‐Modified Bismaleimide Resins
abstract: ABSTRACT Processing methodology critically dictates the crosslinking architecture and macroscopic properties of maleimide copolymer resins. In this work, an allyl‐functional benzoxazine–phthalonitrile resin (DABA‐ph) bearing both oxazine‐ring and phthalonitrile functionalities was employed to modify bismaleimide (BMI) resin via two distinct processing routes: a sequential route (ph‐BD), in which DABA‐ph is grafted predominantly at the chain ends of BMI/DABA prepolymer chains, and a simultaneous route (ph‐B/D), in which DABA‐ph is incorporated in the middle sections of the chains. Systematic characterization by FTIR, DSC, rheology, DMA, TMA, TGA, and mechanical testing reveals that the processing protocol significantly tailors the network microstructure, engendering divergent thermal, mechanical, and thermomechanical performances. Chain‐end grafting (ph‐BD) affords an exceptionally broad low‐viscosity processing window (130°C–210°C) and high flexural strength at low DABA‐ph contents, whereas mid‐chain incorporation (ph‐B/D) enables multipoint crosslinking, delivering higher crosslinking density, high‐temperature modulus, compressive strength, and dimensional stability. Both systems exhibit excellent thermal stability (char yields above 60% at 800°C) and high glass transition temperatures (up to 402°C), surpassing most conventional allyl‐modified BMI resins. This work offers novel insights into processing–structure–property relationships and high‐performance modification strategies for maleimide‐based copolymer resins.

title: Photochemical Oxidation of Thiazolidines and Oxazolidines Enables Access to Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) Sensitive and Chitin‐Derived Heterocycles
abstract: The development of sustainable synthetic methodologies is crucial to advancing greener processes. In this work, a mild and chemoselective photochemical oxidation of thiazolidines to the corresponding thiazolines under an oxygen‐free atmosphere and oxazolidines to oxazolines under an oxygen atmosphere is described. The transformation proceeds efficiently with the inexpensive organophotocatalyst 9‐fluorenone for thiazolidines, while both [Ru(bpy) 3 ](PF 6 ) 2 and 3CzClIPN proved effective for oxazolidines. The reaction tolerates a wide range of functional groups, including oxidation‐sensitive moieties such as dimethylamines and boronic acids, and delivers up to 94% yield across 28 substrates. Importantly, this methodology enables the late‐stage functionalization of the chitin‐derived synthon 3‐acetamido‐5‐formylfuran (3A5F), a challenging aldehyde prone to decomposition, expanding the chemical space of nitrogen‐containing renewable scaffolds. The synthetic utility of the process is further demonstrated through the total synthesis of the antibacterial natural product Aerugine in 20% overall yield. This sustainable and versatile approach opens new avenues for the preparation of heterocycles and bioactive molecules from renewable resources.

title: Rational design of mRNA delivery systems: balancing delivery efficiency and safety toward clinical translation
abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics are expanding from vaccination to cancer immunotherapy, protein replacement, and in vivo gene editing.Across these applications, delivery systems must provide sufficient efficacy in diverse tissues and treatment settings while maintaining acceptable safety.For both lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) and polymeric carriers, delivery efficiency and safety are closely intertwined through charge exposure, membrane activity, and material biopersistence.These material properties facilitate mRNA loading, cellular uptake, and endosomal escape.However, the presence of excessive charges or membrane disruption can induce cell injury and immune activation, whereas prolonged material persistence can increase tissue accumulation and cumulative toxicity.This review presents a shared materials framework for both LNPs and polymeric carriers for mRNA therapeutics.It examines how engineered lipids, alternative surface coatings, and biodegradable or charge-shifting polymers maintain delivery efficiency while reducing carrier-associated safety risks.We further propose practical principles for evaluating mRNA carriers under clinically relevant treatment conditions and for defining an acceptable therapeutic window.Together, this review provides a shared design framework for developing LNPs and polymeric carriers with effective delivery, acceptable safety, and sustained therapeutic benefits.

title: Effects of Two Types of Multi‐Walled Carbon Nanotubes Used for Carbon Fiber Surface Modification on Tensile Properties of Polycarbonate Composites
abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, carbon fibers (CFs) coated with two types of multi‐walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs), manufactured by Nanocyl SA (MWCNT‐a) or TPR Co. Ltd. (MWCNT‐b), were prepared using a reactive polymer, and the effects of the coated MWCNTs on the tensile properties of polycarbonate (PC) composites were investigated. The MWCNT‐coated CFs were prepared through a simple three‐step process. First, a reactive layer of poly(2‐isopropenyl‐2‐oxazoline) (Pipozo) was formed on the CF surface as the first layer. Next, the two MWCNT dispersions were coated onto the Pipozo‐coated CFs to form the second layer. An additional Pipozo layer was then formed as the third layer. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) observations revealed qualitative differences in coating morphology between the two systems. A quantitative analysis showed that the coating amounts of MWCNT‐a and MWCNT‐b were 0.16 ± 0.017 wt.% and 0.12 ± 0.007 wt.%, respectively. The MWCNT‐b system exhibited the highest mean values among the CF‐containing composites. Fracture‐surface SEM revealed PC resin residue on the treated CF surfaces, indicating partial fracture within the adjacent PC matrix. These results suggest that both the Pipozo‐derived interphase and retained MWCNT coating morphology may be important in the interfacial design of CF‐reinforced thermoplastic composites.

title: Heat treatment of railway and heavy machinery grade mild steels: from conventional quenching to smart-nanofluid-assisted cooling
abstract: Abstract Railway-grade mild steel remains a cornerstone material in rail and heavy machinery infrastructure due to its cost-effectiveness and mechanical robustness. However, ensuring optimal hardness, toughness, and wear resistance under demanding service conditions requires intelligent heat treatment strategies. The transformative potential of integrating nanofluid-based quenching and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven optimization in the heat treatment of railway-grade mild steel was explored. We first summarize the influence of critical thermal parameters, such as austenitizing temperature, cooling rate, and quenching medium, on the steel’s microstructure and performance. Particular attention is given to emerging nanofluid quenchants, which enable tunable heat transfer characteristics and improved control over phase transformations. We then examine the role of machine learning (ML) and optimization algorithms in predicting mechanical outcomes, designing process parameters, and reducing trial and error in thermal processing. State-of-the-art applications of deep learning, surrogate modeling, and multi-objective optimization in heat treatment are critically reviewed. Finally, we propose future directions including hybrid intelligent systems, sustainable nanofluid design, and the deployment of digital twins for real-time control in smart manufacturing. This interdisciplinary synthesis provides a roadmap for materials engineers and AI practitioners to co-develop next-generation heat treatment workflows that are efficient, sustainable, and performance-driven, contributing to the evolution of smart railway infrastructure.

title: Biomimetic and Natural Exosomes in Drug Delivery: A Critical Review
abstract: Exosomes are biological nanoparticles (30-150 nm) secreted by most eukaryotic cells. They are composed of a lipid bilayer membrane and an inner compartment that stores various cellular components. In recent years, research on exosomes has grown exponentially due to their biocompatibility, low immunogenicity and cytotoxicity, and their permeability to biological barriers. Among the most promising applications of exosomes are their diagnostic and therapeutic potential, the latter being especially relevant due to their ability to act as a vehicle for drugs. Before exosomes can be applied clinically, it is necessary to optimize the isolation of these nanoparticles from various sources, as well as to carry out their physical and biochemical characterization. Furthermore, their ability to encapsulate molecules with therapeutic effects within them must be perfected. To this end, analytical methods are a key tool for developing each of these steps, and it is essential to understand their principles, strengths, and challenges. In addition, it is necessary to overcome limitations such as the availability of safe sources, the scalability of production, the standardization of isolation, purification, and encapsulation, the inherent heterogeneity of exosomes themselves, the prolongation of in vivo lifespan, and the long-term preservation of these nanoparticles. An alternative is the synthesis of exosome-like nanoparticles, which is less complex but more prone to high production and tailored structure and composition. This review addresses the latest advances in drug delivery focused on exosomes and exosome biomimetic nanoparticles, comparing their advantages and drawbacks from a practical perspective.
