title: Clinical Translation of PEGylated Liposomal Drug Delivery Systems in Oncology
abstract: The development of PEGylated liposome drug delivery systems as a method to deliver nanomedicine in oncology, is a means to improve the pharmacokinetic and therapeutic properties of cytotoxic agents. Liposomes are flexible phospholipid bilayers capable of encapsulating hydrophilic and/or hydrophobic drugs; thereby providing protection to unstable drugs and control over how drugs distribute within the body. Once the surface of liposomes is modified using poly (ethylene glycol) (peg), ‘stealth’ liposomes are formed that demonstrate steric stabilization and inhibit the opsonization of the liposome. As a result of being less susceptible to removal from the circulation by the reticuloendothelial system (RES) due to sterically stabilized surfaces, stealth liposomes will remain in circulation longer than traditional liposomes. Additionally, stealth liposomes will increase the duration in which they remain in proximity to solid tumors through enhanced permeation and retention (EPR) effects. Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin (doxorubicin HCl liposome) and nanoliposomal irinotecan have been the first two liposomal formulations to receive FDA approval. Each formulation provided improvements to the therapeutic index and reduced dose-limiting toxicities relative to their non-pegylated counterparts. However, many obstacles exist that must be addressed prior to widespread adoption of pegylated liposomes. These obstacles include uniform delivery of the liposomes to tumors, ability of liposomes to penetrate into tumor tissue, the “peg dilemma”, and the possibility of eliciting an immune response leading to accelerated blood clearance (ABC) or anti-peg antibodies. Researchers continue to develop novel stealth polymers, PEG-based architectures that respond to stimulus, theragnostic liposomes, and combine liposomes with immunotherapy as methods to achieve more reliable delivery of liposomes and better clinical outcomes for patients. Although pegylated liposomes represent one of the most efficient platforms available for the delivery of chemotherapeutic agents, it is critical to take into consideration both the design of the liposome and the individual characteristics of each patient to obtain optimal results in treating cancers. This revised synthesis explicitly reframes EPR-based deposition as one component of a broader, heterogeneous tumor-transport process; highlights the quantitative limitation that generally less than 2% of the injected nanoparticle dose reaches tumors; incorporates anti-PEG antibody prevalence and patient-stratification considerations; adds manufacturing or CMC reproducibility barriers; and proposes testable translational hypotheses for imaging-guided patient selection and rational immunotherapy combinations.

title: Architecting Organic Electrochemical Transistors for Bioelectronics: From Channel Micro‐Engineering to Microarray Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) have emerged as transformative devices that revolutionize next‐generation electronics to bridge ionic/electronic signaling at the interface between biological and microelectronic systems. This review systematically explores fundamental breakthroughs in OECT channel material engineering and device manufacturing across micro/nanoscales for emerging bioelectronic systems, emphasizing microarchitecture design and patterning strategies that unlock advantages including enhanced transistor performance, high speed, improved mechanical durability, high‐fidelity integration, as well as biocompatibility. We first briefly introduce the device physics underpinning OECTs and state‐of‐the‐art material innovations, focusing on nanostructure‐dominated mixed ionic–electronic conduction. Subsequently, we elaborate on tailored microscale channel architectures, encompassing 1D fibers, 2D micro/nanoporous films, and 3D soft hydrogel networks to address both electronic and mechanical challenges. Furthermore, we highlight advances in scalable fabrication techniques such as printing/photolithography‐based approaches and vertical architectures for developing high‐density flexible OECT arrays. In addition, diverse bioelectronic applications are summarized, including biosensing, signal processing, implantable biointerfaces, and brain‐inspired computing, demonstrating the versatility of OECTs. The discussion concludes by outlining future directions to enhance device reliability and scalability, addressing critical challenges such as material stability and integration complexity. Through this comprehensive analysis, we provide a roadmap for advancing OECT micro/nanotechnology, inspiring future research and accelerating its adoption in bioelectronics.

title: Synthesis and molluscicidal activity of a triazolopyrimidine derivative against Monacha cartusiana
abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND One of the common and harmful pests in Egypt's agroecosystems is Monacha cartusiana , highlighting the need for the development of novel and effective molluscicidal agents for improved control. RESULTS In this study, a novel triazolopyrimidine derivative was prepared using manganese(II,III) oxide (Mn 3 O 4 ) nanoparticles as a heterogeneous catalyst. The synthetic compound showed poor cytotoxicity against HFB4 cells and inhibited CACO‐2 cell growth. It also showed marked antioxidant effects against 2,2‐diphenyl‐1‐picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) and ferric‐reducing antioxidant power (FRAP). Mortality rates of adult and juvenile snails increased with compound concentration and exposure time. For adults, lethal concentrations at 50% (LC 50 ), 25% (LC 25 ), and 10% (LC 10 ) were 0.51%, 0.1275%, and 0.051%, respectively; for juveniles, they were 0.032%, 0.008%, and 0.0032%, respectively. The total hemocyte count of adult snails significantly decreased after 28 days of exposure to LC 25 and LC 10 . Phenoloxidase levels in soft tissue significantly decreased. For antioxidant biomarkers, superoxide dismutase (SOD) significantly decreased, while malondialdehyde (MDA) and glutathione S ‐transferase (GST) significantly increased. After exposure to LC 10 , mild histological abnormalities were observed in digestive gland sections, including vacuolation and necrosis of epithelial cells in some tubule regions; after exposure to LC 25 , serious histological abnormalities, including necrosis of hepatopancreas tubules, were conspicuous. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) showed many ultrastructural abnormalities in the digestive gland of treated snails. CONCLUSION These findings indicate that the synthetic compound exhibits promising molluscicidal activity against M. cartusiana , making it the key result and a potential candidate for further investigation as a molluscicidal agent. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Highly Stable PLA/Gelatin Bionanocomposites for Enhanced Delivery of Chloroaluminum Phthalocyanine for Photodynamic Therapy against SK-MEL-28 Cells
abstract: Abstract This study reports the development of a biodegradable poly(lactic acid) and gelatin (nPLA-G) bionanocomposite as a drug delivery system for chloroaluminum phthalocyanine (ClAlPc) in photodynamic therapy (PDT). Using a hybrid desolvation/emulsification technique, we engineered spherical nanoparticles with an average diameter of 753.3 nm and a positive zeta potential of +8.90 mV. ClAlPc-loaded nanoparticles (nPLA-G/ClAlPc) were prepared using the same process, with a mean diameter of 809.3 nm and a zeta potential of +16.10 mV. The system achieved an exceptional encapsulation efficiency of 90.89% and maintained colloidal stability for over 270 days. In vitro assays showed a pH-dependent release profile, optimizing drug availability in tumoral microenvironments. The nPLA-G/ClAlPc system showed no dark toxicity but reached 97% cytotoxicity in SK-MEL-28 melanoma cells upon light activation (1.0 μmol L–1). These preliminary results demonstrate that the bionanocomposite effectively overcomes ClAlPc hydrophobicity, serving as a promising drug delivery system with preliminary photodynamic efficacy in vitro.

title: Data-driven optimization and multiscale characterization of sustainable epoxy-benzoxazine hybrid composites for high-performance structural applications
abstract: The polymer composites with enhanced mechanical, thermal, and tribological properties are increasingly important for advanced structural applications. In this study, hybrid composites based on an epoxy-benzoxazine matrix reinforced with basalt fibers (BF), waste cotton textile fibers (WCTF), and graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) were developed. Optimization of BF content, WCTF content, GNP loading, and curing temperature for tensile strength, flexural strength, impact strength, and Shore D was performed using a Taguchi L9 experimental design. The optimized composite (30% BF, 10% WCTF, 1% GNPs, and a curing temperature of 160 °C) achieved a tensile strength of 138 MPa, flexural strength of 208 MPa, impact strength of 42 kJ m⁻², and Shore D hardness of 87. In addition, the optimized composite exhibited a storage modulus of 5.2 GPa and a glass transition temperature (Tg) of 132 °C. FTIR, AFM, FESEM with EDS, DMA, DSC, TGA, and wear analyses supported enhanced matrix-reinforcement interactions, improved interfacial adhesion, and favorable thermomechanical and tribological performance. Random Forest and XGBoost machine learning models were created for predicting the composite properties, and XGBoost yielded the highest prediction accuracy (R² = 0.9870–0.993). The proposed experimental, statistical, and machine learning strategy is effective for the design of high-performance epoxy–benzoxazine hybrid composites for applications in structural engineering.

title: PEG-associated efficacy loss in lipid nanoparticles persists across formulation modifications for mRNA delivery
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are clinically proven mRNA delivery vehicles, and repeated administration is often required to maintain therapeutic or prophylactic benefit. However, a single dose can provoke adaptive immune responses against polyethylene glycol (PEG), a polymeric excipient on the LNP surface. In this event, resultant anti-PEG antibodies neutralize subsequent LNP doses, causing efficacy loss and limiting therapeutic utility. Here, we investigated whether altering the LNP formulation between initial and subsequent doses could mitigate PEG-associated efficacy loss. Following the administration of an LNP known to elicit anti-PEG antibodies, we re-dosed with LNPs formulated with varied PEG-lipid chemistry, PEG concentration, mRNA cargo, and administration route. None of these adjustments prevented efficacy loss, which consistently correlated with elevated anti-PEG immunoglobulin M (IgM) and, in some cases, immunoglobulin G (IgG). Reduced PEG concentration diminished immunogenicity but also potency, and intraperitoneal dosing elicited the strongest responses upon repeat injection. Further, LNPs that elicit anti-PEG antibodies also impaired the subsequent delivery of an FDA-approved MC3 formulation, suggesting that anti-PEG immune responses can compromise any PEGylated LNP formulation. Together, these findings demonstrate that PEG-associated efficacy loss cannot be resolved through formulation optimization alone, when the ionizable lipid fails to engage the innate immune receptors TLR4 and CD1d. Instead, they suggest that the ionizable lipid's engagement of innate immune receptors is the primary determinant of repeat dosing success.

title: Synergistic SiO2@DPPA flame retardancy for enhancing flame retardancy and thermal insulation in epoxy resin
abstract: Abstract Novel and environmentally flame-retardant epoxy resin coating that maintain outstanding physical performance are urgently needed for high-tech fields. In this work, SiO 2 @DPPA was successfully synthesized and incorporated together with SiO 2 aerogel and OMMT into EP to prepare EP/SiO₂@DPPA composite coatings. Increasing the SiO 2 @DPPA content progressively enhances the flame retardancy, with a 2wt% SiO 2 @DPPA content yielding the optimal flame retardancy performance for EP. Compared to EP composite coating, the peak heat release rate (pHRR), total heat release (THR) and total smoke production (TSP) values of EP/SiO₂@DPPA composite coatings decreased effectively by 47.6%, 47.6% and 41.5%, respectively. The excellent heat and smoke reduction performance of the composite coatings was further validated through condensed and gas phase flame retardancy mechanism. Moreover, the EP/SiO₂@DPPA composite coatings has good mechanical properties, including the tensile strength of 11.1 MPa. This work further validates the feasibility of preparing flame-retardant high-performance polymer materials by adding organically modified SiO 2 .

title: Synthesis and Polymerization of a Lactone Building Block Derived From Cashew Nut Shells
abstract: The biorenewable feedstock cardanol, a phenol compound substituted with an unsaturated C15 hydrocarbon chain, was selectively transformed into a cyclohexanone derivative through partial hydrogenation. Subsequent conversion via Baeyer-Villiger oxidation (BVO) gave a lactone product (pentadecylcaprolactone, PDCL), which is a mixture of two regioisomers. For the BVO, two variants that are based on either the direct use of a perbenzoic acid as reagent or alternatively the use of a readily available aldehyde in the presence of molecular oxygen as an attractive oxidation reagent have been studied and turned out to be feasible. In addition, suitable work-up has been demonstrated that furnished a sample of the cardanol-derived PDCL-type lactone in 84% isolated yield with 99% purity. Using metal-free polymerization techniques, a PDCL sample has then been readily converted into its homopolymer, which displays a low crystallinity, the latter due to moderate side-chain crystallization. Importantly, in a statistical copolymer with ε-caprolactone (CL), PDCL was shown to be a useful agent to modulate crystallinity, resulting in copolyesters with reduced or very minor crystallinity and accordingly low melting points. For such an effect, typically expensive and fossil-based monomers such as δ-valerolactone (VL) have to be used, highlighting the potential of PDCL for practical application.

title: Integrating chromic responsiveness with conventional performance toward multifunctional smart fibers for applied technologies
abstract: Abstract Stimuli-responsive wearable textiles with reversible colorimetric changes have been crucial for various applications, such as healthcare monitoring, camouflage, energy-saving building materials, and sensing. Rapid technological advancements have led to a diversity of smart wearables that feature fundamentally various reversible colorimetric mechanisms. Different reviews have discussed the recent advancements of chromic materials from unique perspectives. However, reviews focusing on the processing of stimuli-responsive materials are limited. This review surveys the recent progress in the last ten years, exploring the major classes of chromic mechanisms, including electrochromism, mechanochromism, halochromism, thermochromism, and photochromism; the materials and strategies used to develop multifunctional textiles; and the effect of chromic functions on conventional textile performance, such as washability, breathability, mechanical strength, and photostability. Sustainability of chromic fibers focused on natural chromic sources, low-energy processing, biodegradable hosts, and ecological impacts. The design strategies for each category are discussed with a focus on preparation procedures, functional materials, and advanced applications. Moreover, multistimuli-responsive chromic textiles with customizable functionalities are discussed. Challenges and perspectives on the future advancements of smart chromic wearable textiles are proposed. This comprehensive review will provide valuable insights for researchers and scientists in this field.

title: Recent Advances in Performance-Driven Multiscale Strategies for Epoxy-Based Underfill Materials for Advanced Packaging
abstract: The rapid evolution of advanced packaging toward high-density, high-power, and three-dimensional heterogeneous integration has placed increasingly stringent demands on package reliability, particularly because of the thermal expansion mismatch and associated thermomechanical stresses between silicon dies and substrates. Owing to their favorable combination of properties and highly tunable formulation chemistry, epoxy resins remain the predominant matrix materials for underfill applications. However, the design paradigm of epoxy-based underfills is shifting from the optimization of individual thermomechanical properties toward the coordinated regulation of thermal, rheological, mechanical, and reliability-related characteristics. This review summarizes recent advances in epoxy-based underfill materials from the perspectives of thermal management, rheological optimization, mechanical reinforcement, and reliability enhancement, with particular emphasis on the roles of filler engineering, resin and interfacial design, and curing-system regulation. The intrinsic coupling and trade-offs among different performance parameters are also discussed. Furthermore, emerging directions for underfill materials in advanced packaging are outlined, including multiscale structure-property relationships, reliability prediction, and intelligent formulation design. This review aims to provide insights into the synergistic design and practical implementation of high-performance epoxy-based underfill materials for next-generation electronic packaging.

title: The NFIL3-MYC signaling axis: a novel therapeutic target and prognostic marker in high-risk multiple myeloma
abstract: Abstract Background Drug resistance causes tumor relapse, limits the outcomes of patients with high-risk multiple myeloma (MM), and requires the development of targeted therapeutics. Increased Notch signaling promotes drug resistance in high-risk del(17p)/TP53-deficient clonogenic MM cells, highlighting the pathway and its downstream effectors as rational therapeutic targets in aggressive MM. However, the identification of selective, safe, and efficacious inhibitors targeting the Notch pathway remains a substantial challenge. Methods To identify novel druggable Notch effectors, we performed transcriptome profiling of Notch-depleted MM cells and selected potential candidates. We applied functional high-throughput shRNA library screens targeting these genes in MM cells with high Notch activity and under drug selection. Through bioinformatic analysis, we selected NFIL3 and validated its mechanistic specificity using ChIP-seq analysis, immunoblotting, cell viability and growth assays. We targeted NFIL3 via the oleanane-type triterpenoid saponin Raddeanin A (RA) and tested its efficacy in vivo using the murine MOPC.315.BM.Luc.eGFP- mCrbn I391V model. To improve efficacy of RA in vivo, we developed drug-loaded nanocarriers based on polymer micelles. Using patient MM cells with high-risk cytogenetic abnormalities and post B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)-directed immunotherapy, we demonstrated efficacy of RA to circumvent multi-drug resistance. To determine the prognostic significance of NFIL3, we correlated its transcriptional expression with survival data and cytogenetic abnormalities of two patient cohorts. Results In functional genomics screens, we identified NFIL3 as a critical therapeutic vulnerability in high-risk, multidrug-resistant MM. Mechanistic studies silencing NFIL3 revealed that NFIL3 acts as a repressor of the MYC oncogenic driver in MM cells. RA collapsed the MYC-driven transcriptional program essential for MM cell survival and abrogated multidrug resistance of human and murine MM cells in vitro and in vivo. Importantly, the drug RA demonstrated potent anti-myeloma activity in patient-derived cells with high-risk cytogenetics following failure of BCMA-directed immunotherapies. Furthermore, high NFIL3 expression was associated with high-risk cytogenetic abnormalities and extramedullary disease and was verified as an independent prognostic marker for overall survival in MM patients. Conclusions RA targets the NFIL3-MYC axis and demonstrates potent anti-myeloma activity in vivo and in patient-derived high-risk MM cells following failure of BCMA-directed immunotherapies, providing a potent salvage strategy for multi-refractory disease.

title: Poly(2-oxazoline)- and Poly(2-oxazine)-Based Formulation Library Reveals Limits of Solubility Parameter-Based Drug-Polymer Compatibility Prediction
abstract: Abstract Four structurally related poly(2-oxazoline) (POx)- and poly(2-oxazine) (POzi)-based ABA triblock copolymers were evaluated across 21 poorly water-soluble drugs to assess whether Hansen solubility parameters (HSPs) predict polymer-specific formulation performance. HSPs were calculated using Hoftyzer-Van Krevelen (HnV) and Yamamoto molecular break (YMB) methods, with semi-empirical polymer HSPs derived from solvent−solubility profiles. The polymers showed drug-specific performance, with maximum loading capacities exceeding 40 wt % for four drugs and 30 wt % for another four drugs. However, Ra showed limited discriminatory power. Among 20 drugs with YMB-derived Ra values, the lowest-Ra polymer was experimentally best for only 4 (20%), while Ra-based and experimental within-drug pairwise rankings agreed in 59 of 119 comparisons (49.6%). Significant cross-drug correlations for two polymers were positive, opposite to the expected trend. Despite this limited predictive performance, the resulting formulation library provides a broad experimental platform for identifying polymer-drug combinations for subsequent application-specific preclinical development.

title: Tuning Pore Confinement and Chemistry of Fluorine-Free Membranes
abstract: The design of low-temperature fuel cells and electrolyzers involving proton exchange membranes (PEMs) has been dominated by the exceptional performance and industrial dominance of Nafion. With emerging regulations banning the use of fluorinated compounds, the search for F-free alternatives must be accelerated. Here, we optimize a fluorine-free, sustainable, and low-cost liquid crystalline poly(epichlorohydrin)membrane, based on the identification of key descriptors for proton mobility obtained using machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) derived from first-principles calculations for extensive molecular dynamics. Proton transfer is controlled by the interplay between water confinement and internal pore chemistry. This allows us to modify the active functional groups so that they directly participate in the proton diffusion process, increasing three times the diffusion rate in the membrane, thus being closer to Nafion standards. This work provides key descriptors for a targeted design approach essential for catalyzing the commercial development of next-generation fluorine-free PEMs.

title: Nanoparticle-Based Drug Delivery Systems for Anticancer Therapy: Microenvironment-Driven Strategies, Advances, and Challenges
abstract: Cancer remains a major global health challenge, and nanoparticle-based drug delivery systems have emerged as a promising strategy for targeted cancer therapy. However, clinical translation is still limited by an incomplete understanding of how nanoparticles navigate the tumor microenvironment (TME) throughout the delivery process. This review presents an integrated, stage-by-stage framework for nanoparticle design that addresses the TME barriers encountered during systemic circulation, tumor-targeted enrichment, and drug release. During systemic circulation, PEGylation, hydrophilic polymer modification, cell membrane- or exosome-based biomimetic technologies, and biomolecular corona formation are employed to prolong circulation half-life. In the tumor-targeting stage, charge-reversal surfaces, ligand conjugation, ligand shielding, and tuning of physical properties enhance tumor accumulation and cellular internalization. For drug release, molecular and structural design enables intracellular responsive release, stepwise extracellular-to-intracellular release, and sequential release to distinct target cells. Beyond summarizing these strategies, we highlight the newly proposed active transport and retention (ATR) principle as a unifying mechanistic framework that explains how nanoparticles achieve tumor accumulation through active endothelial transport and retention via tumor component interactions. We further discuss translational barriers including complex fabrication, scalability hurdles, and biocompatibility constraints, and outline emerging solutions such as novel nanoparticle fabrication methods (microfluidics, turbulent jet, and microfluidic mixing), engineered biomimetic exosomes, organ-on-a-chip evaluation platforms, and AI-driven design screening. By connecting stage-specific design strategies to the ATR framework, this review offers a mechanistic foundation for the rational design of next-generation nanomedicines.

title: Functional, next-generation, polymeric materials for targeted and controlled drug delivery applications
abstract: Despite their broad clinical use, conventional drug delivery technologies are still limited by inadequate bioavailability, non-specific biodistribution, and uncontrolled drug release, which compromise therapeutic efficacy and safety. With their customizable molecular architecture, physicochemical adaptability, and multifunctional, stimuli-responsive design, next-generation polymeric materials overcome these constraints and allow for precise, site-specific, and regulated therapeutic action. In addition to stimuli-responsive platforms and structurally diverse nanocarriers such as nanoparticles, micelles, dendrimers, polymerases, and nanogels, this review critically examines the molecular and physicochemical design principles, nanoengineering and fabrication strategies, such as self-assembly, microfluidics, and emerging 3D/4D printing. Moreover, the passive, active, and organelle-level targeting mechanisms that govern these systems. In addition to clinical translation challenges, existing research gaps, and emerging directions like sustainable polymer chemistry, AI-driven design, adaptive 4D-printed systems, and personalized therapeutics, their disease-specific applications in cancer, neurological, cardiovascular, and infectious diseases, chronic wound healing, and regenerative medicine are critically evaluated. When taken as a whole, next-generation polymeric materials provide a flexible, clinically translatable platform for accurate, effective, and safe therapeutic intervention. However, they also highlight the crucial issues that need to be addressed in order to expedite clinical translation.

title: One‐Step Synthesis of a Phosphaphenanthrene–Imidazole Phosphorus–Nitrogen Flame Retardant for Epoxy Thermosets: Degradation Pathway and Fire‐Safety Mechanism
abstract: ABSTRACT Epoxy resins (EPs) possess excellent mechanical strength, chemical resistance, and adhesion, yet their inherent flammability limits their use in fire‐sensitive applications. Under increasingly stringent safety requirements, developing simple and scalable halogen‐free flame retardants remains a significant challenge. In this work, a phosphorus–nitrogen flame retardant, 6‐(2‐(1H‐imidazol‐1‐yl)ethyl)dibenzo[c,e][1,2]oxaphosphinine 6‐oxide (DIM), was synthesized via a one‐step nucleophilic addition reaction between 9,10‐dihydro‐9‐oxa‐10‐phosphaphenanthrene‐10‐oxide (DOPO) and 1‐vinylimidazole (VIM), and subsequently incorporated into epoxy thermosets, either alone or in combination with melamine (MEL). Fourier‐transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) was used to evaluate the formation of DIM. The thermal degradation, fire performance, char structure, phosphorus retention, and evolved products of the resulting thermosets were investigated using thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), cone calorimetry, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Raman spectroscopy, X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP‐OES), TGA coupled with Fourier‐transform infrared spectroscopy (TG‐FTIR), and pyrolysis‐gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (Py‐GC/MS). Changes in the characteristic FTIR bands of the PH and vinyl groups, together with the retention of the DOPO and imidazole frameworks, supported the formation of the proposed addition product. Among the investigated formulations, EP/DIM‐MEL4 exhibited the greatest improvement in fire performance, with reductions of 31.9% and 36.0% in peak heat release rate and total heat release, respectively, relative to neat EP. Microscopic and spectroscopic analyses indicated the formation of a more expanded, continuous, and structurally ordered protective char. ICP‐OES analysis showed that approximately 31.1% of the initial phosphorus was recovered in the solid residue. TG‐FTIR and Py‐GC/MS further suggested that volatile phosphorus‐containing species contributed to gas‐phase radical inhibition, whereas nitrogen‐containing volatiles derived from the imidazole moiety and MEL contributed to flame‐zone dilution. Overall, the improved fire safety of the DIM‐containing epoxy thermosets is attributed to the combined effects of gas‐phase inhibition and condensed‐phase barrier formation. This work provides a simple strategy for developing DOPO‐based phosphorus–nitrogen flame‐retardant systems for epoxy thermosets.

title: Plasma Protein Association with High Drug-Loaded Polymer Micelles: An Atomistic Molecular Dynamics Study
abstract: Abstract Polymeric micelles are widely studied drug delivery platforms whose interactions with plasma proteins influence in vivo performance. However, the combined effects of non-pEG hydrophilic coronas and high drug loading on protein adsorption remain poorly understood. We performed all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the association of three plasma proteins: apolipoprotein E (ApoE), human serum albumin (HSA), and immunoglobulin G (IgG), with curcumin-loaded ABA triblock copolymer micelles. To isolate corona effects, micelles shared an hydrophobic core chemistry and differed only in the hydrophilic A-block: poly(ethylene glycol) (pEG), poly(N,N-dimethylacrylamide) (pDMAA), or poly(sarcosine) (pSAR). Two drug loadings (20% and 60% drug/polymer mass ratio) were examined. Binding was assessed via contact areas, hydrogen bonds, and interaction energies. pEG micelles showed the strongest protein association. pDMAA and pSAR exhibited weaker, surface-limited interactions. These simulations provide molecular-level insight into protein adsorption on drug-loaded polymeric micelles and compare alternative hydrophilic A-blocks to pEG.

title: Surface and interfacial characteristics of similar and dissimilar adhesively bonded metal joints after post-bonding moisture exposure
abstract: This work investigates the effects of post-bonding moisture exposure on the multiscale bonding behavior of both similar and dissimilar adhesively bonded metal joints, using AA6061–AA6061 and AA6061–DP590 Double Cantilever Beam (DCB) joints as examples. The investigated moisture exposure significantly reduced the bonding performance of both joints, as reflected by reductions in peak load and failure displacement, and changed the failure mode from dominant cohesive failure in the adhesive for as-received joints to dominant interfacial failure after post-bonding moisture exposure. Such interfacial failure can occur microscopically within the oxide layer, as demonstrated by the damage path across the oxide layer and along the interface between the oxide layer and the adhesive. This phenomenon was attributed to moisture-induced restructuring of the oxide layers due to oxidation and hydration, which weakened the oxide layers on both metal surfaces. Detailed investigation of the surface chemistry and oxide layers on metal surfaces after moisture exposure provided insightful results for studying surface modification methods, such as plasma and laser treatments, to mitigate moisture-induced degradation of metal joints.

title: Syntheses, structural characterization and catalytic studies of N^O-donor (pyrazolyl-phenoxy)imine transition metal complexes in ethylene oligomerization reactions
abstract: The transition metal complexes of the general formula [Co (L1) 2 ] (Co1), [ Pd (L1) Cl] (Pd1), [ Ni (L1) 2 ] (Ni1) , and [ Ni (L2) 2 ] (Ni2) prepared by the reactions of the appropriate CoCl 2 , Pd(NCMe) 2 Cl 2 , and NiCl 2 metal precursors with the respective pyrazolyl-phenoxy-imine ligands; ((2-(3,5-dimethyl-1H-pyrazol-1-yl)ethylimino)methyl)naphthalen-2-ol (HL1) and ((2-(3,5-phenyl-1H-pyrazol-1-yl)ethylimino)methyl)naphthalen-2-ol (HL2) . The new compounds were structurally characterized using NMR and FT-IR spectroscopies, mass spectrometry, elemental analyses, and single crystal X-ray crystallography. The molecular structure of Ni2 depicts two bidentate (N^O) HL2 ligands around the nickel(II) metal center to form rare diamagnetic square planar complexes. On the other hand, ligand HL1 displays a tridentate N^N^O coordination to palladium(II) to give a mono-ligated palladium(II) complex Pd1 , consistent with the theoretically optimized structures using Density Functional Theory (DFT). Upon activation with EtAlCl 2 as a co-catalyst, complexes Co1, Pd1, Ni1 , and Ni2 form active catalysts in ethylene oligomerization reactions to produce mainly C 4 and C 6 oligomers, depending on the co-catalyst used. While the use of EtlAlCl 2 forms C 4 and C 6 oligomers, MAO and Me3Al results in the dimerization reactions to afford mainly C 4 oligomers. Both the catalytic activities and product selectivity were controlled by the nature of the metal complex and reaction conditions. For example, the nickel-based complexes displayed higher catalytic activities of up to 46 120 g product mol –1 Ni h –1 compared to the other metal complexes. Similarly, the use of Ni2 /EtAlCl 2 catalyst system displayed the highest catalytic activity compared to the Ni2/ AlMe 3 and Ni2 /MAO systems.

title: Smart Interactive System for the Enhanced Bioimaging and Multi‐Drug Synergistic Therapy in Tumor‐Microenvironment
abstract: ABSTRACT Tumor microenvironment (TME) interactive platforms are promising for accurate diagnostics and therapeutics. Herein, a smart interactive system (G⊂H) consisting of a hypoxia‐acid dual triggered multifunctional guest (G) and an amphipathic metal‐organic capsule (H) was successfully established for bioimaging and treatment. Hydrophobic G is encapsulated in cavity of H to form the homogeneous soluble G⊂H, which enhances its accumulation in tumor cells, controls the interactive regulation between G⊂H and TME, and facilitates the sensitivity of tumor cell therapy. When triggered in TME, G⊂H selectively releases an alkylating agent and a doxifluridine (DFUR) via the activation of azo and ketal linkers for multidrug chemotherapy, and the fluorescence emission from the activated G⊂H is used for real‐time release visualization of the hypoxia‐activating drug in cell substructure and hypoxia imaging. Owing to its homogeneous delivery, TME regulation and TME response properties toward the hypoxia tumor cells, G⊂H exhibits significantly higher toxicity in a hypoxic environment (0.1% O 2 ) than that in normoxia. As expected, G⊂H performs good imaging capability and treatment effect in hypoxia tumor cells, flow cytometry assay and tumor‐bearing mice, implying its great potential in bioimaging and multidrug synergistic therapy.

title: The self-assembly, hydrogel properties and application of thiolated chitosan
abstract: Chitosan was the second most abundant natural polymer, existing in exoskeleton and crustaceans. Chitosan was insoluble in water and most organic solvents. Its solubility was dependent on its deacetylation degree, molecular weight, ionic strength and temperature. Since the discovery of thiolated chitosan, numerous studies have certificated its notable properties, including adhesiveness, biocompatibility, in-situ gel properties, and controllable drug release. This review discussed the physicochemical properties and preparation for chitosan, which could help us understand the bioactivity of thiolated chitosan. The features of chitosan materials, especially its application scope have been expanded through thiolation modification. The self-assembly effects of thiol modification on its viscoelasticity and gelation properties were explored via hydrogel features. Rheological study of thiolated chitosan was available to observe the crosslinking structure, viscoelasticity, gel-points, fluidity and mechanical behaviors. Meanwhile, applications of thiolated chitosan in antibacterial materials, drug carriers, tissue engineering and agriculture were also explored. In addition to conventional biological applications, thiolated chitosan could also be effectively used for pollutant treatment and air water harvesting. This review provided significant conclusions and prospects for the application of thiolated chitosan.

title: Simultaneous Quantification of Dispersant Adsorption and Pesticide Solubilization by UV –Vis Spectrophotometry Combined With Chemometrics
abstract: ABSTRACT In pesticide suspension concentrate formulations, interfacial adsorption of dispersants onto active‐ingredient particles and solubilization of pesticide molecules by dispersant micelles frequently coexist; however, analytical methods capable of simultaneously characterizing these interfacial and bulk‐phase processes remain limited. Herein, a multivariate calibration strategy combining ultraviolet–visible (UV–Vis) spectrophotometry with partial least squares (PLS) regression and competitive adaptive reweighted sampling (CARS) was developed. The method enabled simultaneous determination of residual tristyrylphenol ethoxylates (TSPEO) and prometryn in processed supernatants, allowing TSPEO adsorption to be quantified indirectly by mass balance. In the hold‐out validation set, the CARS model incorporating single‐component (SC) spectra achieved coefficients of determination for validation ( R 2 val ) of 0.9965 and 0.9904 and root mean square errors of prediction (RMSEP) of 6.1471 and 1.0129 mg/L for TSPEO and prometryn, respectively. Prometryn predictions also showed good agreement with high‐performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) measurements. Application of the method showed that wet milling increased the Langmuir‐derived apparent maximum adsorption capacity of TSPEO from 4.02 to 13.18 mg/g, whereas the nonmilled system exhibited linear micellar solubilization of prometryn above the critical micelle concentration (CMC), with a weight solubilization ratio (WSR) of 0.0291 g/g. These results provide a quantitative framework for investigating coupled dispersant adsorption and pesticide solubilization in suspension concentrate systems.

title: Steric Stabilization of Lipid Nanoparticles by Sequence-Defined Polymer−Lipids Enhances Gene Expression
abstract: Abstract Polyethylene glycol (PEG) conjugated lipids are frequently used for the design of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) in the field of gene therapy. However, conventional PEG−lipids contain a distribution of polymer chain lengths. To overcome this limitation, we have prepared a structurally defined PEG-alternative polymer-lipid platform synthesized via solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS), enabling precise control over polymer chain length and lipid anchor identity. A library of chain-length-defined poly(succinamide−4,7,10-trioxatridecane)n−lipid (poly(SA-TTD)n-lipid) conjugates, with hydrophilic polymer segments ranging from 923 to 2133 g/mol and varied lipid tails, was synthesized and formulated into DNA-loaded LNPs using microfluidic mixing. Systematic variation of polymer length and lipid tail structure revealed their distinct influence on NP size, colloidal stability, and DNA encapsulation efficiency. All formulations produced particles with narrow size distributions (PDI <0.2) with efficient DNA association. In vitro studies demonstrated that selected PEG-alternative LNPs significantly enhanced transfection efficiency compared to PEG2000-containing controls, achieving up to 18-fold higher transgene expression. Notably, these formulations also exhibited an approximately fourfold higher endosomal escape-associated signal. In vivo evaluation in zebrafish larvae (ZFL) further confirmed efficient systemic circulation and superior transgene expression without apparent toxicity. In summary, this work establishes a modular, sequence-defined polymer-lipid platform that provides a promising PEG alternative for LNP-mediated gene delivery.

title: Morpholine: A multifaceted compound influencing industries through history and innovation
abstract: The exploration of chemicals essential to various industries has a long and rich history, beginning with naturally derived substances in early human civilization. Over time, the development and use of synthetic chemicals have revolutionized key sectors such as pharmaceuticals, agriculture, textiles, and more. Morpholine, a versatile heterocyclic compound, exemplifies this evolution through its broad industrial applications, stemming from its unique structure and chemical adaptability. This review presents a comprehensive overview of the structure, methods of obtaining morpholine, its physicochemical properties, and the wide range of its derivatives. Through an in-depth analysis, it highlights the critical role of morpholine in advancing innovation and progress across diverse scientific and industrial domains.

title: Thermally programmed disassembly and reconstruction of 2D polymer platelets via melting-governed crystallization-driven self-assembly
abstract: Abstract Crystallization-driven self-assembly (CDSA) has emerged as a powerful methodology to precisely control the morphology and size of polymer nanostructures, enabling the formation of 1D and 2D nanomaterials. Yet, the melting behavior of polymer crystals grown in solution using this technique has remained largely unexplored. Here, we show that melting temperature is a structurally sensitive descriptor and an active design parameter for 2D poly(ε-caprolactone) platelets formed by seeded living CDSA. Using nano differential scanning calorimetry, we establish quantitative thickness-melting correlations consistent with Gibbs-Thomson theory for finite, solution-grown lamellae. Leveraging these insights, we engineer multilayer platelets with programmed thermal stability gradients that undergo rapid, selective disassembly under mild conditions (37 °C), yielding uniform hollow architectures within minutes. Upon cooling, released polymer chains undergo spatially confined recrystallization, allowing reversible reconstruction and self-healing of the platelet framework. This work establishes melting as a powerful thermodynamic handle for probing and reconfiguring CDSA-derived nanostructures in solution.

title: Parameter Optimization of HDI ‐Mediated Chain Extension for High‐Performance PBAT : A Superior Alternative to Conventional Melt Polycondensation
abstract: ABSTRACT The production of high‐molecular‐weight poly(butylene adipate‐co‐terephthalate) (PBAT) via conventional melt polycondensation is severely hampered by high melt viscosity, thermal degradation, and energy‐intensive processing. This work systematically investigates the chain extension of PBAT with hexamethylene diisocyanate (HDI) via reactive melt‐mixing to address these limitations. We elucidated the effects of precursor molecular weight, HDI content, and processing temperature on the structural and mechanical properties of the resulting PBAT. Under optimal conditions within the investigated range (PBAT‐2.0h precursor, 1.0 wt% HDI, 190°C), chain‐extended PBAT (PBAT‐2.0h‐HDI) achieves high molecular weight ( M n = 63,304 g/mol), high tensile strength (33.4 ± 2.1 MPa), and super elongation at break (1764.7% ± 112.6%). Crucially, comparative analysis reveals that PBAT‐2.0h‐HDI outperforms PBAT synthesized via prolonged direct polycondensation (PBAT‐4.5h) in both molecular weight and mechanical properties, while greatly reducing the total reaction time and acid value. The mechanism involves the formation of high‐molecular‐weight linear chains and a few long‐chain branching structures. As far as we know, the systematic investigation into how precursor PBAT molecular weight governs the structure and properties of chain‐extended PBAT is first reported in this study. This work establishes comprehensive structure–property correlations for HDI‐mediated PBAT chain extension, delivering low‐energy, short‐cycle technical guidance for the production of high‐performance biodegradable PBAT.

title: Synthesis of Monofunctional Benzoxazine Resin Containing Acetylamino Group and Properties of Its Copolymer With Epoxy Resin
abstract: ABSTRACT This study reports the design and synthesis of a novel amide‐functionalized monofunctional benzoxazine (TaPBA) and its incorporation into epoxy resin to develop high‐performance thermosetting networks with significantly enhanced overall properties. The structure of TaPBA was proved by Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FT‐IR) and proton Nuclear Magnetic Resonance ( 1 H NMR). The curing behavior of EP‐TaPBAresins wereanalysed by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and FT‐IR, revealing that TaPBA played a positive role in reducing the curing temperature of EP‐TaPBA resins. Meanwhile, the enlarged free volume within the crosslinked polymer network effectively suppressed dielectric polarization, resulting in reduced dielectric constant and dielectric loss. However, the addition of TaPBA also reduced the initial decomposition temperatures ( T 5% and T 10% ) and glass transition temperature ( T g ) of EP‐TaPBA resins. In conclusion, this research conducted a detailed analysis on the curing behavior, thermal stability and dielectric properties of TaPBA‐modified epoxy resins, which has certain reference value for related work.

title: Biomaterial-Enabled Delivery Strategies to Overcome Treatment Resistance in Medulloblastoma
abstract: Abstract: Multimodal therapy has improved survival in medulloblastoma (MB), yet recurrence, neuraxis dissemination, and treatment-related late effects remain major challenges. Treatment resistance reflects clonal evolution, drug efflux, altered DNA-damage and apoptotic responses, treatment-persistent cells, the tumor microenvironment, and inadequate active-drug exposure across the blood-brain barrier (BBB), postoperative residual compartments, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) spaces. Biomaterials can modify intracranial distribution, local retention, combination exposure, and intracellular cargo release. This review evaluates direct MB evidence for polymeric and lipid nanomedicines, biomimetic and virus-derived platforms, magnetic materials, extracellular vesicles, and hydrogels across intracranial solid lesions, postoperative residual disease, and neuraxis dissemination, while defining the limits of extrapolation from related tumors. Systemic nanomedicines currently provide the broadest evidence chain from formulation optimization to brain or tumor exposure, target modulation, and antitumor activity. Disease-matched studies also support active transendothelial transport and intrathecal nanoparticle therapy for metastatic MB. Most evidence remains preclinical; direct evidence of reversal of established treatment resistance is limited, and human studies largely assess route feasibility and safety. Progress will require quantitative active-cargo pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, disease- and route-matched models, juvenile neurodevelopmental safety testing, and defined product quality attributes to determine whether these platforms can widen the therapeutic window or restore treatment sensitivity. Keywords: medulloblastoma, treatment resistance, biomaterials, nanomedicine, translational medicine

title: The Pictet‐Spengler and Bischler‐Napieralski Reactions and Their Variants: Ever‐Green and Ever‐Evolving Processes for the Construction of Diverse Heterocyclic Ring Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT The Pictet‐Spengler and Bischler‐Napieralski reactions together with most of the variants described herein have been known for well over a century and throughout this time they have provided an exceptional means for the preparation of a wide range of heterocyclic compounds, most notably isoquinoline and β‐carboline derivatives. The versatility of these reactions is becoming ever more apparent not least because of the increasingly mild and selective means now available for effecting them. Furthermore, the biomimetic nature of the Pictet‐Spengler reaction together with the discovery of enzymes that catalyze these, both in vivo and in vitro, has further enhanced their utility and their prospects for ever more expansive deployment. This article seeks to provide an integrated overview of the title reactions that is cast in an historical perspective but with a focus on contemporary examples that attempt to highlight the dynamic nature of the activities in the field. The literature up to 2025 is covered with an emphasis on more recent and significant advances.

title: From Molecular Targets to Advanced Delivery Systems: Aptamers for Precision Ocular Therapeutics
abstract: ABSTRACT Ocular disorders, ranging from anterior surface diseases to posterior segment pathologies present significant challenges and opportunities in therapeutic delivery. The unique anatomical and physiological barriers of the eye demand precision therapeutics that go beyond the limitations of traditional biologics. Aptamers, often termed “chemical antibodies,” have emerged as a transformative class of therapeutics, that circumvents these barriers. This review analyses critical molecular targets across major ocular diseases for example TNF‐a, MMP9, and chemokines in dry eye disease; TGFβ2, GD15 in glaucoma; VEGF and complement components in age related macular degeneration and diabetic retinopathy as foundations for next generation aptamer‐based therapeutic and diagnostic design. It also highlights the latest advancements in sustained‐release delivery systems to address persistent challenges in ocular pharmacology, including overcoming ocular barriers, preventing rapid clearance, and improving bioavailability. Furthermore, the review addresses current translational barriers, including nuclease degradation, rapid ocular clearance, and complex regulatory hurdles that must be navigated to bring these therapies to clinical practice. As research progresses toward identifying disease‐specific signatures, the high tunability and customization of aptamers offer a promising avenue for revolutionizing interventions in complex ocular conditions, ultimately signalling a shift toward more personalized and effective eye care.

title: Neuropathic Pain Comorbid Cognitive Impairment and Vitamin D: A Narrative Review From Mechanisms to Clinical Management
abstract: Neuropathic pain (NP) is not merely simple persistent pain but a complex pathological condition mediated by dysregulation across multiple systems, including the neuro-immune-endocrine axis. As a high-intensity endogenous stressor, persistent pain signals can deplete cognitive resources and trigger neuroinflammation and central sensitization, leading to cognitive impairment (CI) characterized by attention deficits and impaired working memory. Currently, mainstream pharmacological treatments for NP carry risks of addiction and may exacerbate CI. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop synergistic intervention strategies that address both pain management and cognitive protection. Given that NP and CI share multiple pathological pathways, identifying interventions capable of simultaneously targeting multiple mechanisms has become a research hotspot. Vitamin D, a secosteroid hormone with both neuroprotective and immunoregulatory functions, is closely associated with an increased risk of NP and CI when deficient. Existing evidence suggests that Vitamin D may regulate the shared pathological mechanisms of these two diseases through multiple pathways, thus serving as a potential adjunctive strategy worthy of further investigation to alleviate the intertwined vicious cycle between NP and CI. This paper systematically reviews the shared pathological mechanisms between NP and CI, summarizes the latest research progress, and explores the multi-target mechanisms of Vitamin D in intervening in NP-CI comorbidity, aiming to promote the application of this safe and cost-effective nutritional strategy in dietary supplementations for NP-CI comorbidity.

title: Examining Plasma Polymer‐Coated Indium Tin Oxide Slides to Enhance Analyte Detection in Matrix‐Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization Mass Spectrometry Imaging
abstract: Analyte delocalization is a significant challenge in matrix‐assisted laser desorption/ionization (MALDI) mass spectrometry imaging (MSI). In this study, we present a novel approach to decrease this phenomenon and improve analyte detection by modifying the wettability of indium tin oxide (ITO)‐coated glass slides, commonly used for tissue analysis, using plasma polymer coatings. These coatings are stable under vacuum conditions and during the ionization process. Surface coatings had minimal impact on the signal‐to‐noise ratio of peptides, proteins, and lipids in profiling experiments, where analytes were directly spotted on the surface, but it had a pronounced effect in MALDI MSI. When analyzing fresh‐frozen murine brain sections, the highly hydrophobic pPFO coating reduced analyte delocalization and improved the detection of m/z features and lipids compared to uncoated ITO slides. This enhancement was likely due to better preservation of native spatial distribution during tissue‐dependent extraction and retention. Notably, cholesterol, a critical analyte in brain research, was easily detected. This study marks the first application of plasma polymers to modify ITO slides for MALDI MSI, resulting in a significant enhancement of localized lipid ion intensity, particularly in the context of high‐resolution MALDI‐2.

title: Mercury(II) Salts‐Mediated Transformations of Acetylene Systems: Synthetic Perspectives
abstract: ABSTRACT This mini‐review presents recent advances in the transformation of acetylenic compounds mediated by mercury(II) salts. Hg(II) salts serve as both catalysts and stoichiometric reagents in these transformations. Despite their toxicity, Hg(II) salts are inexpensive, stable, and demonstrate high reactivity toward alkynes. Their versatile reactivity enables the synthesis of organomercury compounds (OMCs), heterocyclic compounds containing various heteroatoms, and selected analogues of natural products. OMCs represent an important class of organometallic compounds. They have been used as intermediates or model compounds for studying the fundamental mechanisms of various reactions, particularly mercuration of alkynes and heterocyclic compounds, as well as mercuric intermediate transmetallation and iododemercuration. Recent studies have reported the synthesis of mono‐ and bi‐nuclear OMCs with novel structures containing bithiazole, triazole, benzimidazole, coumarin, and piperidine moieties. Among the Hg(II) salts investigated for the cyclization and hydration of substituted alkynes, mercury(II) triflate has demonstrated high catalytic efficiency and broad applicability. Its effectiveness has been reported in several types of alkyne transformations. This review also summarizes the reactions of various nucleophiles with acetylenic compounds under Hg(II)‐mediated electrophilic activation. Particular attention is given to the regioselectivity of these reactions and the factors that control the formation of the corresponding products.

title: Recent advances in surface modification of nanocellulose by chemical routes
abstract: Nanocellulose (NC) is one of the great inventions of the late twentieth century that may address some of the recent challenges regarding environmental sustainability. NC has great potential in a multitude of applications, such as medicine, sensors, automotive, electronics and many others due to its origin from renewable sources, excellent mechanical resistance, biocompatibility, and biodegradability. For most of these applications, NC's surface must be chemically modified to meet the specific requirements of each intended use. The presence of hydroxyl groups at its surface opens plenty of possibilities for tuning its surface properties by chemical reactions. However, choosing the most suitable method in terms of efficiency, simplicity, health and environmental risks, costs, etc. requires thorough research of the existing literature which is extremely voluminous. The review proposed herein aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the recent efforts, progress, and challenges in the chemical surface modification of NC as cellulose nanocrystals, nanofibrillated cellulose and bacterial cellulose for imparting new properties to nanocelluloses for cutting-edge applications. The goals of this review reside in selecting relevant papers on this topic especially from the last decade, in order to provide a critical description of the methods used for the chemical modification of NC and an objective comparison between the results reported by different authors when applying similar methods. Particular attention was paid to the presentation of the novelties that different methods brought in terms of increasing efficiency, reducing toxicity, simplifying the procedures, or enlarging the spectrum of NC's applications.

title: Design and optimization of mucoadhesive chitosan microspheres for oesophageal delivery of fluconazole
abstract: Background Oesophageal candidiasis remains challenging to treat owing to rapid transit of conventional oral formulations through the oesophagus, resulting in inadequate local drug delivery and reduced therapeutic efficacy. To address these limitations, the present study aimed to develop fluconazole-loaded chitosan microspheres (FCZ-CMs)-based orodispersible tablets (ODTs) that rapidly disintegrate in the oral cavity while releasing mucoadhesive microspheres capable of adhering to oesophageal mucosa, enabling sustained localized drug delivery. Methods FCZ-CMs were developed by the emulsion cross-linking method using a 2 3 full factorial design to optimize particle size (PS), entrapment efficiency (EE), drug release (DR), and ex vivo oesophageal retention (ORT). Optimised FCZ-CMs (F9) were extensively characterized by Infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), X-ray diffractometry (XRD), and in vitro drug release studies. Further, the ODTs developed by direct compression of F9 were evaluated for wetting time (WT), disintegration time (DT), drug content (DC), % drug release at 60 min (%DR), similarity ( f 1 /f 2 ), and stability under real-time and accelerated conditions. Results The optimised FCZ-CMs (F9) exhibited a PS (31.81 ± 1.14 μm), EE (84.12% ± 2.15%), DR (58.46% ± 1.89% at 60 min), and ORT (51.22% ± 2.11% at 30 min), demonstrating excellent suitability for localized oesophageal delivery. FTIR confirmed drug–polymer compatibility, SEM revealed spherical microspheres with a crenated surface morphology favourable for mucoadhesion, while DSC and XRD demonstrated reduced crystallinity of FCZ within the chitosan matrix. The ODTs loaded with F9 displayed high DC (99.14% ± 0.58%), short WT (19.62 ± 0.51s), and DT (23.83 ± 0.86s). The dissolution profile of ODTs remained comparable to that of F9 ( p > 0.05 ), with drug release of 53.16% ± 1.24% at 60 min and similarity factor ( f 2 = 80) and difference factor ( f 1 = 8 ), confirming that the compression process did not significantly alter the release behaviour of the optimised microspheres. The formulation also remained stable under both real-time and accelerated storage conditions. Conclusion The optimised ODTs successfully translated the performance of FCZ-CMs into a patient-friendly, oesophageal-targeted drug delivery system without compromising their controlled-release or mucoadhesive characteristics. The use of a simple, reproducible, and scalable direct compression process, together with preservation of microsphere functionality following tablet compression, highlights the translational potential of this platform for localized treatment of oesophageal candidiasis and deserves further clinical investigation.

title: Phenylboronic acid-functionalised gelatin/PVA films for enhanced vaginal mucoadhesion and sustained metronidazole release
abstract: This study aimed to develop gelatin films with enhanced mucoadhesive retention and controlled metronidazole (MTZ) release for vaginal drug delivery. Gelatin was functionalised with 4-formylphenylboronic acid (FPBA) via Schiff base formation followed by reductive amination to obtain derivatives with different functionalisation levels (Gel-Bor L, Gel-Bor M and Gel-Bor H). Structural changes in gelatin were confirmed by 1 H NMR and FTIR spectroscopy, while pH-dependent electrophoretic mobility revealed a shift in the isoelectric point towards lower pH values following derivatisation. Films were prepared by solvent casting using PVA as a film-forming excipient and characterised in terms of thickness, surface pH, folding endurance, transparency, thermal stability and puncture resistance. Ex vivo mucoadhesion of NaFl-loaded films was assessed on freshly excised sheep vaginal mucosa using a flow-through wash-off assay in vaginal fluid simulant (VFS, pH 4.0). In vitro MTZ release was evaluated using Franz diffusion cells, while cytocompatibility was assessed in HT-29 cells and MSCs using the CCK-8 assay. Gel-Bor/PVA films were uniform, flexible and compatible with simulated vaginal pH. Compared with PVA-only and gelatin/PVA controls, Gel-Bor/PVA films exhibited markedly improved mucosal retention, with Gel-Bor L/PVA and Gel-Bor M/PVA performing comparably to chitosan. Chemical modification of gelatin also prolonged MTZ release: after 16 h, cumulative release decreased from 73.10% for gelatin/PVA to 66.50%, 60.40% and 51.70% for Gel-Bor L/PVA, Gel-Bor M/PVA and Gel-Bor H/PVA, respectively. No cytotoxic effects were detected under the tested conditions for all Gel-Bor/PVA formulations. Overall, this chemical modification transformed gelatin-based films into mucoadhesive, cytocompatible platforms with sustained MTZ release for vaginal application.

title: Surface-Mediated Immunomodulation by Electrostatic Immobilization of Naproxen on Plasma-Aminated Poly(ε-caprolactone) Films Rescues Osteogenic Differentiation via Attenuation of NF-κB Signaling
abstract: Chronic inflammation following biomaterial implantation often leads to fibrous encapsulation and compromised osseointegration, particularly in clinically inflamed environments. We developed a surface-functionalized poly-(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) platform to modulate the early inflammatory microenvironment via surface-mediated drug release. PCL films were aminated by plasma polymerization, enabling the electrostatic immobilization of naproxen. Surface characterization by zeta potential analysis, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and atomic force microscopy (AFM) confirmed successful amine functionalization and subsequent naproxen loading. The functionalized films exhibited a pronounced early burst release of naproxen within the initial hours after immersion, addressing the early phase of post-surgical inflammation. In vitro studies using MC3T3-E1 pre-osteoblasts under lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced inflammatory conditions showed that naproxen released from the surface significantly reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion, including IL-6 and IL-1β. The cytokine-suppressive effect of the naproxen-functionalized surface was further supported by mechanistic experiments showing that soluble naproxen attenuated LPS-induced NF-κB p65 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation. These results suggest that the anti-inflammatory response mediated by surface-released naproxen is, at least in part, attributable to the intrinsic NF-κB-modulating activity of naproxen. Modulation of the inflammatory microenvironment restored osteogenic differentiation, with increased expression of RUNX2, ALP, and OPN, and enhanced matrix mineralization, as confirmed by Alizarin Red S staining. These findings demonstrate that surface-mediated delivery of naproxen enables temporally controlled osteoimmunomodulation and supports osteogenic function under inflammatory stress, underscoring the potential of this surface-engineering strategy for bone-regenerative applications.

title: Layer‐by‐Layer Core–Shell Nanoparticles Encapsulate HDAC Inhibitors and Reduce Diffuse Midline Glioma Neurosphere Proliferation
abstract: ABSTRACT Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) is a central nervous system (CNS) tumor that is often surgically inaccessible and radiation‐resistant. Preclinical studies have suggested the utility of histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitors for this challenging disease. However, clinical trials with the HDAC inhibitor panobinostat have not demonstrated a survival benefit, largely due to insufficient drug concentration at the tumor site after oral administration. The blood‐brain barrier limits the CNS penetration of the drug, and off‐target drug toxicity precludes increasing systemic doses. The present study develops a lipid‐polymer nanoparticle (NP) for targeted HDAC inhibitor delivery to DMG tumor cells. NPs with an acid‐terminated PLGA core and a soy PC and POPG lipid shell were found to display suitable properties for systemic administration and efficiently encapsulate panobinostat and quisinostat. Layer‐by‐layer modification with electrostatically charged layers of poly‐L‐arginine, followed by hyaluronate (HA) significantly increased NP association with patient‐derived DMG tumor neurospheres in vitro. Furthermore, HA‐layered panobinostat NPs retained HDAC inhibition activity and reduced the proliferation of DMG neurospheres. These results demonstrate the potential of this optimized NP for targeted delivery of HDAC inhibitors to DMG with an improved tumor exposure‐to‐off‐target toxicity ratio.

title: Green MW/US‐Assisted Construction of Pyrano[2,3‐b]pyridines and Pyrazolo[3,4‐d]pyrimidinones: Pathway Control and Antibacterial Evaluation
abstract: A green, activation-controlled route was examined for the preparation of biologically relevant fused N/O heterocycles, with particular emphasis on whether the mode of energy delivery can redirect the reaction pathway. A single hydrazine-derived precursor was treated with acetic anhydride under the same nominal temperature and reaction time while applying ultrasound (US), microwave (MW), or combined MW/US activation. The three modes led selectively to different annulated products: pyrazolo[3,4-d]pyrimidinone 5 was isolated in 88% yield under US, oxazinyl-pyrazolidinone 6 in 85% yield under MW, and the more extensively fused derivative 7 in 85% yield under combined MW/US conditions. These results indicate that pathway selection can be influenced by the physical manner in which energy is supplied without altering the reagent set. The products were assigned from FT-IR, NMR, EI-MS, and elemental-analysis data and were screened against representative Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Compound 5 gave the best overall antibacterial response, including a 32.0 ± 0.6 mm inhibition zone against Staphylococcus aureus and MIC values of ≤ 12.5 µg/mL. Its experimental performance was consistent with favorable docking contacts and stable molecular-dynamics behavior, while DFT/Mulliken analysis provided a rationale for the reactive sites involved in annulation and dehydration.

title: Synthesis and Characterization of Polyvinyl Alcohol Cross‐Linked Mercaptosuccinic Acid Pendant Cardanol‐Based Polybenzoxazines Incorporating ZrO 2 Nanoparticles for Proton Exchange Membranes
abstract: ABSTRACT This study reports on the synthesis of cross‐linked networks of cardanol‐based polybenzoxazine (MCBZ) having pendant 2‐mercaptosuccinic acid with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) to create hydrophilic polymer membranes. These membranes were further reinforced with varying weight percentages of zirconium oxide nanoparticles (ZrO 2 NPs) for proton transport membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) applications. The nanocomposites were characterized using FT‐IR, 1 H NMR, 13 C NMR, PXRD, FE‐SEM, and HR‐TEM analyses. Their physicochemical characteristics such as swelling ratio (SR), water uptake (WU), and ion‐exchange capacity (IEC) were systematically assessed. Among the prepared nanocomposite membranes, the membrane with 5 wt% ZrO 2 ‐dispersed PVA/MCBZ showed an optimal IEC of 1.5 meq g −1 and a proton conductivity of 1.096 × 10 −1 S/cm at 110°C. Arrhenius plots indicated low activation energies, suggesting efficient proton transport through the vehicular mechanism. The stability of membranes was estimated through Fenton's reagent testing at 80°C, which showed minimal chemical degradation. The ZrO 2 /PVA/MCBZ membrane demonstrated an improved maximum power density of 0.802 mW cm −2 at a current density of 2.26 mA cm −2 , surpassing the 0.530 mW cm −2 achieved by the PVA/MCBZ membrane at 1.19 mA cm −2 . Based on these results, the composite membranes show promising potential as membrane materials for fuel‐cell applications.

title: Spiropyran‐Crosslinked PDMS Optical Waveguides for Pressure Sensing and Visual Cue of Localized Pressure Threshold
abstract: ABSTRACT Compliant optical waveguides are promising candidates for stress/strain sensing in soft robotics and personalized healthcare. While poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) offers a robust platform, enhancing sensitivity and integrating localized visual indicators for pressure threshold detection remains an active area of research. In this study, spiropyran (SP)‐crosslinked PDMS optical waveguides are fabricated to provide quantitative low‐pressure sensing alongside a reversible colorimetric response upon reaching localized stress/strain thresholds. Using a three‐factor Box–Behnken design, the interplay between SP concentration, PDMS mixing ratio, and curing conditions is systematically mapped across four key properties: transverse compression sensitivity (up to 100 kPa), secant modulus, refractive index (RI), and propagation loss. Response surface methodology reveals that the mixing ratio primarily drives the optomechanical response, whereas SP concentration significantly impacts RI and propagation loss. At higher transverse compressions (0.9–2.4 MPa), mechanochromic activation (SP‐to‐merocyanine isomerization) correlates directly with the macroscopic strain‐hardening regime, providing thresholds comparable to human tissue bruising. Although no single formulation simultaneously maximizes low‐pressure sensitivity and mechanochromic performance while minimizing optical attenuation, standout combinations are identified for specific application scenarios. These results establish a robust, polymer‐science‐based framework for the rational design of multifunctional, mechanochemically active optical pressure sensors.

title: Effect of an Ultra‐Low Content of Reactive Polyhedral Oligomeric Silsesquioxane on Structure and Thermal Properties of Polycyanurate/Polybenzoxazine Hybrid Nanocomposites
abstract: ABSTRACT In this work, a comprehensive investigation of the co‐curing behavior, chemical transformations during network formation, and thermal properties of dicyanate ester of bisphenol E (DCBE)/benzoxazine (BZ) (75/25 wt.%) systems modified with epoxycyclohexyl‐functionalized polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (ECH‐POSS) was carried out to establish the role of the reactive nanofiller in the structure and properties of hybrid organic–inorganic polycyanurate (PCN)/polybenzoxazine (PBZ)/ECH‐POSS nanocomposites. DSC revealed a complex three‐stage curing process and demonstrated that ECH‐POSS selectively accelerated the cyanate ester component, while only weakly affecting BZ polymerization. At 2 wt.% ECH‐POSS, the curing onset decreased from 113°C to 91°C, the main exothermic peak shifted from 241°C to 220°C, the induction period decreased by ∼28%, and the reaction rate at a fixed heating time increased more than threefold. FTIR and 1 H/ 1 3 C NMR analyses provided evidence for chemical coupling between DCBE and BZ through the formation of triazine, iminocarbonate, and carbamate structures. Incorporation of only 0.025–0.5 wt.% ECH‐POSS dramatically increased the glass transition temperature ( T g ) of hybrid nanocomposites by 14°C–21°C, reaching 214°C at 0.025 wt.% ECH‐POSS. They retained high thermal stability and char yields of 43%–44% at 790°C. These results demonstrate that reactive ECH‐POSS effectively allows for combining lower‐temperature curing with substantial T g enhancement, providing a promising strategy for the design of high‐performance thermosetting nanocomposites.

title: A recyclable g-C3N4/Biochar@Pd hybrid nanocatalyst for high-performance Suzuki, Stille and CN coupling reactions
abstract: To make progress in green chemistry, it is important to use stable heterogeneous catalysts from sources that can be reused. Biochars have attracted much attention for their sustainability and environmental friendliness. However, the general application of these compounds in C C and C N cross-coupling reactions catalyzed by palladium remains to be achieved. In this study, a new nanocatalyst g-C 3 N 4 /Biochar@Pd with stability and catalytic efficiency has been prepared for the cross-coupling reactions. The catalyst was prepared by thermal polycondensation (first step) and supported on the surface of palladium (last step). Then, its properties were investigated by FT-IR, XRD, SEM, TEM, EDX, ICP-OES, BET and TGA techniques. The catalyst performance was investigated in C N, Suzuki, and Stille coupling reactions. In the C N reaction, arylamines were obtained in 83–96% yields. In the Suzuki and Stille reactions, yields of 83–98% were obtained, depending on the substrate. The reactivity order of the halides was I > Br > Cl, and electron-donating groups increased the reaction rate. The g-C 3 N 4 /Biochar@Pd nanocatalyst was reused in five consecutive cycles. This indicates that the catalyst is stable and can be effectively used in cross-coupling reactions.

title: Applications of the Ritter reaction in the synthesis of biologically active compounds: A review
abstract: Nitrogen-containing compounds play a fundamental role in biological systems. Proteins, the essential macromolecules responsible for virtually all cellular functions, are composed of amino acids linked through amide (peptide) bonds, highlighting the critical importance of nitrogen-containing functionalities in life processes. Ritter reaction methodologies have provided access to novel amide-containing scaffolds, which are valuable in medicinal chemistry and the creation of drug libraries. Ritter reactions are widely used in the synthesis of highly functionalized heterocycles, fused heterocycles and linear amides. These classes of compounds exhibit notable biological activities, including antibacterial, antiviral, antiproliferative, and anticancer activities. This review aims to compile recent advancements and applications of the Ritter reaction and mainly focuses on synthetic strategies for the synthesis of different classes of bioactive compounds. The evaluation of potential therapeutic applications of the most promising molecules synthesized using Ritter reaction is also covered in the present review.

title: Thermomechanical and Combustion Behavior of Post Cured Allyl and Furan Functionalized Bio‐Based Benzoxazine Composites
abstract: ABSTRACT Bio‐based benzoxazines represent a promising class of high‐performance thermosets for sustainable composite applications. Nonetheless, their thermomechanical characteristics are frequently not as robust as those found in traditional fossil‐derived materials. This study systematically investigates the influence of allyl and furan functional groups, on the crosslinking behavior and thermomechanical performance of bio‐based polybenzoxazine composites, with particular emphasis on the role of post curing. Allyl and furan groups were selected for their bio‐based origins and distinct crosslinking mechanisms: allyl groups undergo thermally induced radical crosslinking to enhance network stiffness, while furan moieties provide high aromatic content and electrophilic reactivity to increase crosslink density and thermal stability. Two benzoxazine monomers based on 4,4′‐diaminodicyclohexylmethane Ph‐dcda (phenol‐based), and AllylPh‐dcda (allylphenol‐based) were synthesized and compared with the commercially available furan functionalized FB602. Fiber‐reinforced polymers were manufactured via compression moulding using recycled carbon fiber nonwovens as reinforcement. The effects of post curing at 220°C on network formation, thermomechanical properties, and combustion behavior were evaluated revealing that post curing significantly enhanced the crosslink density ( V e ) for all systems. The structural effects, however, varied substantially depending on the functional groups present. For poly(AllylPh‐dcda), post curing nearly doubled the storage modulus and increased V e by a factor of 1.8, attributed to thermally activated crosslinking of allyl bonds as compared to non‐post‐cured samples. Poly(FB602) exhibited the highest V e and a substantial increase in glass transition temperature ( T g ) from 169°C to 203°C upon post curing, owing to the high aromatic content and furan mediated crosslinking. In contrast, poly(Ph‐dcda), lacking additional reactive functionalities, underwent network degradation during post curing, resulting in a decreased gel content. Combustion analysis demonstrated that functionalized benzoxazines exhibited reduced peak heat release rates and shorter burning times, compared to non‐functionalized systems, although all composites failed the UL‐94 vertical burning test, highlighting the limitations in flame retardancy. Future studies should focus on incorporating flame retardant additives to improve fire safety compliance. This work elucidates the structure property relationships governing crosslinking efficiency and thermomechanical performance in functionalized biobased polybenzoxazines, providing guidance for the rational design of sustainable high‐performance composites.
